title.zh: 卷一百五十八 列傳第四十五: 姚樞 許衡 竇默
title.en: Volume 158 Biographies 45: Yao Shu, Xu Heng, Dou Mo
title.raw: 卷一百五十八 列傳第四十五: 姚樞 許衡 竇默 Volume 158 Biographies 45: Yao Shu, Xu Heng, Dou Mo

sentences.zh: 姚樞，字公茂，柳城人，後遷洛陽。

translations.literal: Yao Shu, courtesy name Gongmao, was a native of Liucheng and later moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shu, whose courtesy name was Gongmao, came from Liucheng and later settled in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 少力學，內翰宋九嘉識其有王佐略，楊惟中乃與之偕覲太宗。

translations.literal: In youth he studied strenuously; Hanlin Academician Song Jiujia recognized that he possessed the capacity of a chief minister, and Yang Weizhong thereupon took him along to have an audience with Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied with great diligence. The Hanlin academician Song Jiujia saw in him the makings of a statesman, and Yang Weizhong brought him to an audience with Taizong.

sentences.zh: 歲乙未，南伐，詔樞從惟中即軍中求儒、道、釋、醫、卜者。

translations.literal: In the yiwei year, during the southern campaign, an edict ordered Shu to follow Weizhong to the army to seek out scholars of Confucianism, Daoism, and Buddhism, as well as physicians and diviners.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year, when the court launched its southern campaign, Shu was ordered to accompany Weizhong to the army and recruit Confucian, Daoist, and Buddhist scholars, along with physicians and diviners.

sentences.zh: 會破棗陽，主將將盡坑之，樞力辨非詔書意，他日何以復命，乃蹙數人逃入篁竹中脫死。

translations.literal: When Zaoyang was taken, the commanding general was about to bury all the captives alive; Shu forcefully argued that this was not the intent of the imperial edict and asked how one could report back on another day—thereupon he gathered several men who fled into bamboo thickets and escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: When Zaoyang fell, the commander was about to massacre the prisoners. Shu argued strenuously that this was not what the edict intended and asked how they could answer for it later. He then gathered a few men, hid them in bamboo groves, and saved them from death.

sentences.zh: 拔德安，得名儒趙復，始得程頤、硃熹之書。

translations.literal: When De'an was captured, he obtained the eminent scholar Zhao Fu and for the first time gained access to the works of Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: After De'an was taken he came upon the renowned scholar Zhao Fu and, through him, first obtained the writings of Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，賜金符，為燕京行台郎中。

translations.literal: In the xinchou year he was granted a gold tally and appointed Director in the Yanjing Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinchou year he received a gold tally and was made a director in the Yanjing regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時牙魯瓦赤行台，惟事貨賂，以樞幕長，分及之。

translations.literal: At that time Yaruqachi headed the secretariat and cared only for bribes; because Shu was chief of staff, a share reached him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yaruqachi then headed the secretariat and dealt only in bribes. As chief of staff, Shu was offered his share as well.

sentences.zh: 樞一切拒絕，因棄官去。

translations.literal: Shu refused everything and thereupon resigned his office and left.
translations.idiomatic: Shu refused every offer and resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 攜家來輝州，作家廟，別為室奉孔子及宋儒周惇頤等象，刊諸經，惠學者，讀書鳴琴，若將終身。

translations.literal: He brought his family to Huizhou, built a family temple, and set up a separate hall with images of Confucius and Song scholars such as Zhou Dunyi; he printed the classics, aided students, read books and played the zither, as though he would spend his life thus.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his family to Huizhou, built a family temple, and set up a separate hall with images of Confucius and Song masters such as Zhou Dunyi. He printed the classics, helped students, and passed his days reading and playing the zither, as if he meant to live out his life in retirement.

sentences.zh: 時許衡在魏，至輝，就錄程、硃所注書以歸，謂其徒曰：「曩所授受皆非，今始聞進學之序。」

translations.literal: At that time Xu Heng was in Wei; he came to Huizhou, copied the annotated books of Cheng and Zhu to take home, and told his disciples: "What I received and transmitted before was all wrong; only now do I hear the proper sequence for advancing in learning."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Heng was then in Wei. He came to Huizhou, copied Cheng's and Zhu's commentaries to take home, and told his students, "Everything I had learned and taught before was mistaken. Only now do I understand the proper path of study."

sentences.zh: 既而盡室依樞以居。

translations.literal: Thereupon his entire household came to live with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he brought his whole household to live with Shu.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛邸，遣趙璧召樞至，大喜，待以客禮。

translations.literal: When Shizu was still in his princely residence, he sent Zhao Bi to summon Shu, was greatly pleased upon his arrival, and treated him with the courtesy due a guest.
translations.idiomatic: While Kublai was still heir apparent, he sent Zhao Bi to summon Shu. Delighted at his arrival, he received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 詢及治道，乃為書數千言，首陳二帝三王之道，以治國平天下之大經，彙為八目，曰：修身，力學，尊賢，親親，畏天，愛民，好善，遠佞。

translations.literal: When asked about the way of governance, he composed a memorial of several thousand characters, first setting forth the Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings as the great constant for ordering the state and bringing peace to all under Heaven, which he gathered into eight headings: cultivate the self, study strenuously, honor the worthy, cherish kin, revere Heaven, love the people, delight in goodness, and keep far from flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about governance, he wrote a memorial of several thousand characters. He began with the Way of the legendary sage rulers as the foundation for ruling the realm, then set out eight principles: self-cultivation, diligent study, honoring the worthy, cherishing kin, revering Heaven, loving the people, delighting in goodness, and keeping flatterers at a distance.

sentences.zh: 次及救時之弊，為條三十，曰：「立省部，則庶政出一，綱舉紀張，令不行於朝而變於夕。

translations.literal: Next he addressed the abuses of the age and set forth thirty articles, saying: "If provincial ministries are established, then the myriad affairs will issue from one source, the guiding rope will be raised and the mesh spread, and orders will not fail to be issued at court yet change by evening.
translations.idiomatic: He then listed thirty reforms to remedy the ills of the day. "Establish central ministries," he wrote, "so that government issues from a single source, policy is coordinated, and orders issued at court are not overturned overnight.

sentences.zh: 辟才行，舉逸遺，慎銓選，汰職員，則不專世爵而人才出。

translations.literal: Recruit men of ability, raise the reclusive and overlooked, be careful in selection and appointment, and reduce redundant offices—then hereditary rank alone will not hold sway and talent will emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit the capable, raise the overlooked, scrutinize appointments, and trim redundant posts—then office will not depend on hereditary privilege alone and talent will come forward.

sentences.zh: 班俸祿，則贓穢塞而公道開。

translations.literal: Institute graded salaries, and corruption will be blocked while the public Way opens.
translations.idiomatic: Pay regular salaries, and bribery will be checked while fair government becomes possible.

sentences.zh: 定法津，審刑獄，則收生殺之權於朝，諸侯不得而專，丘山之罪不致苟免，毫髮之過免罹極法，而冤抑有伸。

translations.literal: Fix the laws, examine criminal cases carefully—then the power of life and death will be gathered in the court, feudatories will not be able to monopolize it, crimes as great as hills will not escape through indulgence, faults as slight as a hair will not suffer extreme punishment, and the wrongfully oppressed will obtain redress.
translations.idiomatic: Codify the laws and review criminal cases carefully, so that the power of life and death rests with the court and local lords cannot claim it for themselves. Great crimes will not be lightly pardoned, minor faults will not draw extreme penalties, and the wrongfully condemned will find justice.

sentences.zh: 設監司，明黜陟，則善良姦窳可得而舉刺。

translations.literal: Establish supervisory commissioners and make promotions and dismissals clear—then the worthy and the corrupt can be distinguished and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint supervisory commissioners with clear authority to promote and dismiss, so that the worthy and the corrupt can be identified and brought to account.

sentences.zh: 閣徵斂，則部族不橫於誅求。

translations.literal: Suspend levies and collections, and the tribes will not run riot in exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Halt arbitrary levies, and the tribes will no longer prey on the people with demands and punishments.

sentences.zh: 簡驛傳，則州郡不困於需索。

translations.literal: Streamline the courier system, and the prefectures and commanderies will not be worn down by requisitions.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the burden of the courier service, and the provinces will not be exhausted by constant demands.

sentences.zh: 修學校，崇經術，旌節孝，以為育人才、厚風俗、美教化之基，使士不媮於文華。

translations.literal: Restore schools, honor the classics, and commend filial piety and chastity as the foundation for nurturing talent, strengthening custom, and beautifying instruction, so that scholars do not grow slack in literary cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Restore schools, honor the classics, and commend filial piety and chastity as the foundation for nurturing talent and improving morals, so that scholars do not neglect learning for mere display.

sentences.zh: 重農桑，寬賦稅，省徭役，禁遊惰，則民力紓，不趨於浮偽，且免習工技者歲加富溢，勤耕織者日就飢寒。

translations.literal: Emphasize agriculture and sericulture, lighten taxes, reduce corvée labor, and forbid idleness—then the people's strength will be eased, they will not rush toward empty artifice, and one will avoid the situation in which those who learn crafts grow richer year by year while those who diligently plow and weave daily approach hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Promote farming and sericulture, lighten taxes, reduce corvée, and forbid idleness, so that the people are relieved and do not chase vain pursuits—and so that artisans do not grow rich while honest farmers and weavers sink into want.

sentences.zh: 肅軍政，使田裡不知行營往復之擾攘。

translations.literal: Rectify military administration so that the countryside does not know the turmoil of camps coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline the armies so that the countryside is no longer disturbed by marching camps.

sentences.zh: 周匱乏，卹鰥寡，使顛連無告者有養。

translations.literal: Relieve the destitute and comfort widows and orphans, so that those in extremity with none to appeal to have support.
translations.idiomatic: Relieve the destitute and care for widows and orphans, so that those with nowhere to turn are provided for.

sentences.zh: 布屯田以實邊戍，通漕運以廩京都。

translations.literal: Deploy garrison farming to fill the border defenses and open grain transport by canal to fill the granaries of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Establish frontier garrisons and military farms to strengthen the borders, and open canal transport to supply the capital.

sentences.zh: 停債負，則賈胡不得以子為母，破稱貸之家。

translations.literal: Halt debt bondage, and merchant foreigners will not be able to treat interest as principal and ruin households that lend on interest.
translations.idiomatic: Ban debt slavery, so that foreign merchants cannot compound interest upon interest and destroy families who lend at usury.

sentences.zh: 廣儲蓄、復常平以待凶荒，立平準以權物估，卻利便以塞幸途，杜告訐以絕訟源。」

translations.literal: Expand reserves, restore the Ever-Normal Granaries to await famine years, establish the Equitable Standard to regulate prices, repel profit-seeking convenience to block paths of favor, and stop malicious accusations to cut off the source of litigation."
translations.idiomatic: Build up reserves, restore ever-normal granaries against famine, regulate prices through state purchasing, curb profiteering, and stop malicious denunciations that breed endless lawsuits."

sentences.zh: 各疏施張之方，其下本末兼該，細大不遺。

translations.literal: Under each item he set forth methods of implementation; below them root and branch were both covered, nothing great or small omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Under each heading he explained how to carry it out, covering both principles and details without omission.

sentences.zh: 世祖奇其才，動必召問，且使授世子經。

translations.literal: Shizu marveled at his talent, summoned him whenever he moved, and also had him instruct the heir in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai admired his ability, consulted him on every important matter, and had him teach the classics to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 壬子夏，從世祖徵大理，至曲先腦兒之地。

translations.literal: In the summer of the renzi year he followed Shizu on the campaign against Dali, reaching the place called Quxiannao'er.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the renzi year he accompanied Kublai on the campaign against Dali as far as Quxiannao'er.

sentences.zh: 夜宴，樞陳宋太祖遣曹彬取南唐不殺一人、市不易肆事。

translations.literal: At a night banquet Shu related how Song Taizu sent Cao Bin to take the Southern Tang without killing a single person and without disturbing the markets.
translations.idiomatic: At an evening banquet Shu told how Emperor Taizu of Song had sent Cao Bin to conquer the Southern Tang without killing a soul or disturbing the markets.

sentences.zh: 明日，世祖據鞍呼曰：「汝昨夕言曹彬不殺者，吾能為之，吾能為之！」

translations.literal: The next day Shizu, gripping his saddle, cried out: "What you said last night about Cao Bin not killing—I can do that, I can do that!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Kublai gripped his saddle and cried, "What you said last night about Cao Bin—I can do the same, I can do the same!"

sentences.zh: 樞馬上賀曰：「聖人之心，仁明如此，生民之幸，有國之福也。」

translations.literal: Shu, from horseback, congratulated him: "The heart of a sage, benevolent and clear thus—this is the good fortune of the living people and the blessing of the state."
translations.idiomatic: From horseback Shu congratulated him: "With a heart so benevolent and clear, the people are blessed and the realm is fortunate."

sentences.zh: 明年，師及大理城，飭樞裂帛為旗，書止殺之令，分號街陌，由是民得相完保。

translations.literal: The next year the army reached the city of Dali; he ordered Shu to tear cloth into banners, inscribe the order to halt killing, and post them throughout the streets and lanes, whereby the people were able to preserve one another intact.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the army reached Dali. He had Shu cut cloth into banners bearing orders to spare lives and post them through the streets, so that the people were able to protect one another.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，樞入見。

translations.literal: In the bingchen year Shu had an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingchen year Shu was received in audience.

sentences.zh: 或讒王府得中土心，憲宗遣阿藍答兒大為鉤考，置局關中，以百四十二條推集經略宣撫官吏，下及徵商無遺，曰：「俟終局日，入此罪者惟劉黑馬、史天澤以聞，餘悉誅之。」

translations.literal: Some slandered the princely residence for winning the hearts of the Chinese heartland; Mongke sent Alan Dar to conduct a great inquisition, established a bureau in Guanzhong, and under one hundred forty-two articles gathered together the officials of pacification commissions and pacification offices, down to tax merchants without exception, saying: "When the inquiry ends, of those who fall under these charges only Liu Heima and Shi Tianze are to be reported; all the rest are to be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Some accused the prince of winning over the Chinese territories. Mongke sent Alan Dar to conduct a sweeping investigation in Guanzhong under one hundred forty-two charges, implicating every pacification official and tax merchant. He declared, "When the inquiry ends, only Liu Heima and Shi Tianze are to be reported to me; all others are to be executed."

sentences.zh: 世祖聞之不樂。

translations.literal: Shizu heard of this and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was deeply troubled when he heard this.

sentences.zh: 樞曰：「帝，君也，兄也；

translations.literal: Shu said: "The Emperor is both sovereign and elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "The emperor is both your sovereign and your elder brother;

sentences.zh: 大王為皇弟，臣也。

translations.literal: the Great Prince is the imperial younger brother, a subject.
translations.idiomatic: you are the imperial younger brother and a subject.

sentences.zh: 事難與較，遠將受禍。

translations.literal: The matter is hard to contest; in the end you will suffer disaster.
translations.idiomatic: This is not a quarrel you can win; in the end you will come to harm.

sentences.zh: 莫若盡王邸妃主自歸朝廷，為久居謀，疑將自釋。」

translations.literal: Better to send all the consorts and ladies of the princely residence to return to court of their own accord, planning for a long stay—suspicion will then release itself."
translations.idiomatic: Better to send your consorts and household to court voluntarily and plan for a long stay there—suspicion will then lift of its own accord."

sentences.zh: 及世祖見憲宗，皆泣下，竟不令有所白而止，因罷鉤考局。

translations.literal: When Shizu met Mongke, both wept; in the end he was not allowed to make any explanation before it stopped, and the inquisition bureau was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai met Mongke they both wept. He was never allowed to plead his case, yet the investigation was called off and the inquisition bureau dissolved.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，立十道宣撫使，以樞使東平。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne he established pacification commissioners for ten circuits and appointed Shu pacification commissioner for Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: After Kublai ascended the throne he created pacification commissioners for ten circuits and appointed Shu to Dongping.

sentences.zh: 既至郡，置勸農、檢察二人以監之，推物力以均賦役，罷鐵官。

translations.literal: Once he reached the commandery he appointed two men for encouraging agriculture and inspection to supervise it, assessed material resources to equalize levies and corvée, and abolished the iron monopoly office.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his jurisdiction he appointed overseers for agriculture and inspection, assessed property to distribute taxes and corvée fairly, and abolished the iron monopoly.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜太子太師。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign he was appointed grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 樞曰：「皇太子未立，安可先有太師？」

translations.literal: Shu said: "The imperial heir has not yet been established—how can there first be a Grand Preceptor?"
translations.idiomatic: Shu objected, "The crown prince has not yet been named—how can there be a grand preceptor before that?"

sentences.zh: 以所受制還中書，事見《許衡傳》。

translations.literal: He returned the commission he had received to the Central Secretariat; the affair is recorded in the biography of Xu Heng.
translations.idiomatic: He returned his commission to the Central Secretariat; the affair is described in the biography of Xu Heng.

sentences.zh: 改大司農。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 樞奏曰：「在太宗世，詔孔子五十一​​代孫元措仍襲封衍聖公，卒，其子與族人爭求襲爵，訟之潛籓，帝時曰：'第往力學，俟有成德達才，我則官之。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: "In Taizong's time an edict ordered Kong Yuancuo, fifty-first-generation descendant of Confucius, to continue inheriting the enfeoffment as Duke Yansheng; when he died his son and clansmen contended for the succession and brought suit to the princely residence, whereupon the Emperor at the time said: 'Just go and study strenuously; when you have achieved virtue and outstanding talent, I will give you office.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized: "Under Taizong, Kong Yuancuo, fifty-first-generation descendant of Confucius, was confirmed as Duke Yansheng. After his death his son and kinsmen fought over the title and appealed to Your Highness's residence. You then said, 'Go and study hard; when you have proven virtue and talent, I will appoint you.

sentences.zh: '又曲阜有太常雅樂，憲宗命東平守臣輦其歌工舞郎與樂色俎豆至日月山，帝親臨觀，飭東平守臣，員闕充補，無輟肄習。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Qufu there is the elegant music of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Mongke ordered the Dongping magistrate to transport its singers, dancers, musicians, and ritual vessels to Riyue Mountain, and the Emperor personally came to observe, instructing the Dongping magistrate to fill any vacancies and not interrupt practice.
translations.idiomatic: Qufu also preserves the court ritual music. Mongke had the Dongping magistrate bring its singers, dancers, musicians, and ritual vessels to Riyue Mountain, where you watched in person and ordered vacancies filled so practice would never lapse.

sentences.zh: 且陛下閔聖賢之後《詩》、《書》不通，與凡庶等，既命洛士楊庸選孔、顏、孟三族諸孫俊秀者教之，乞真授庸教官，以成國家育材待聘風動四方之美。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty pitied that descendants of the sages did not know the Book of Songs and Book of Documents and were the equal of commoners; having already ordered the Luoyang scholar Yang Yong to select promising grandsons of the Kong, Yan, and Meng clans to teach them, I beg that Yong be truly appointed instructor, to fulfill the state's beauty of nurturing talent, awaiting appointment, and moving all four quarters by its influence.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty also pitied Confucius's descendants who could not read the classics and were no better than commoners. You have already ordered Yang Yong of Luoyang to select promising youths from the Kong, Yan, and Meng clans for instruction. I ask that Yong be formally appointed instructor, so that the state may truly nurture talent and set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 王鏞煉習故實，宜令提舉禮樂，使不致崩壞。」

translations.literal: Wang Yong is versed in former precedents and ought to be ordered to direct rites and music so that they do not fall into ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong is steeped in ritual precedent and should be put in charge of rites and music so they do not fall into decay."

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every recommendation.

sentences.zh: 詔赴中書議事，及講定條格，且勉諭曰：「姚樞辭避台司，朕甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him to the Central Secretariat to discuss affairs, and when statutes were drafted and settled the Emperor also exhorted him, saying: "Yao Shu declined the high offices of the secretariat—I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the Central Secretariat to deliberate on policy and help draft statutes. The emperor also encouraged him, saying, "Yao Shu declined high office at the secretariat, and I greatly commend him for it.

sentences.zh: 省中庶務，須賴一二老成同心圖贊，其與尚書劉肅往盡乃心，其尚無隱。」

translations.literal: The myriad affairs within the secretariat must rely on one or two seasoned men of the same mind to plan and assist; go with Minister Liu Su and exhaust your hearts—still, do not hold back."
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat's daily business needs one or two seasoned men working in concert. Go with Minister Liu Su and give your full counsel—hide nothing."

sentences.zh: 及修條格成，與丞相史天澤奏之，帝深嘉納。

translations.literal: When the revision of statutes was completed, together with Chancellor Shi Tianze he presented them, and the Emperor deeply approved and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: When the statutes were finished, he presented them with Chancellor Shi Tianze, and the emperor warmly approved them.

sentences.zh: 李璮謀叛，帝問：「卿料何如？」

translations.literal: When Li Tan plotted rebellion, the Emperor asked: "What do you reckon?"
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tan plotted rebellion, the emperor asked, "What do you expect of him?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「使璮乘吾北征之釁，瀕海搗燕，閉關居庸，惶駭人心，為上策。

translations.literal: He replied: "If Tan seized the opening of our northern campaign, raided Yan along the coast, and closed Juyong Pass, terrifying men's hearts—that would be the upper stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "His best move would be to strike while we are campaigning in the north—raid Yan from the coast, close Juyong Pass, and spread panic. That would be the upper stratagem.

sentences.zh: 與宋連和，負固持久，數擾邊，使吾罷於奔救，為中策。

translations.literal: To ally with Song, hold out stubbornly for a long time, and repeatedly harass the borders, wearing us out in constant rescue—that would be the middle stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Allying with Song, holding out stubbornly, and harrying our borders until we exhaust ourselves in relief—that would be the middle stratagem.

sentences.zh: 如出兵濟南，待山東諸侯應援，此成擒耳。」

translations.literal: If he marched out from Jinan and waited for the feudatories of Shandong to come to his aid, that would be capture made certain."
translations.idiomatic: If he marched from Jinan and waited for the Shandong lords to rally to him, he would be as good as captured."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今賊將安出？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Which stratagem will the rebel now adopt?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Which course will he take?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「出下策。」

translations.literal: He replied: "He will adopt the lower stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The lower one."

sentences.zh: 初，帝嘗論天下人材，及王文統，樞曰：「此人學術不純，以遊說乾諸侯，他日必反。」

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had once discussed talent throughout the realm, and when Wang Wentong was mentioned Shu said: "This man's learning is impure; he uses persuasion to seek favor with feudatories—one day he will rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor had discussed talent under Heaven and Wang Wentong's name came up, Shu said, "His learning is impure and he wins favor with lords through persuasion. One day he will rebel."

sentences.zh: 至是，文統果因璮伏誅。

translations.literal: At this time Wentong indeed, on account of Tan, was executed in secret.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wentong had indeed been executed for his part in Tan's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜中書左丞，奏罷世侯，置牧守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and memorialized to abolish hereditary marquisates and establish prefectural and commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became left vice director of the Central Secretariat and memorialized to abolish hereditary fiefs and appoint regular prefectural governors.

sentences.zh: 或言中書政事大壞，帝怒，大臣罪且不測者，樞上言：

translations.literal: Someone said the affairs of the Central Secretariat were greatly ruined; the Emperor was angry, and ministers faced unpredictable punishment—Shu submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that the secretariat's administration had collapsed, the emperor flew into a rage and ministers faced unknown punishments. Shu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 太祖開創，跨越前古，施治未遑。

translations.literal: Taizu opened the founding, surpassing all former ages, yet had no leisure to put governance in order.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu founded the dynasty on a scale surpassing all earlier ages, yet had no time to put full governance in place.

sentences.zh: 自後數朝，官盛刑濫，民困財殫。

translations.literal: From the several reigns that followed, offices multiplied and punishments ran wild; the people were distressed and finances exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In the reigns that followed, offices multiplied, punishments ran wild, the people suffered, and the treasury was drained.

sentences.zh: 陛下天資仁聖，自昔在潛，聽聖典，訪老成，日講治道。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's natural endowment is benevolent and sage; from of old while still in the princely residence you listened to the sacred classics, sought out the seasoned, and daily discussed the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is benevolent and sage by nature. Even while still heir apparent you studied the classics, sought out seasoned advisers, and discussed governance every day.

sentences.zh: 如邢州、河南、陝西，皆不治之甚者，為置安撫、經略、宣撫三使司。

translations.literal: Such places as Xingzhou, Henan, and Shaanxi, where misrule was most severe, were given the three commissions of pacification, strategic pacification, and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In badly governed regions such as Xingzhou, Henan, and Shaanxi you established pacification, strategic pacification, and regional pacification commissions.

sentences.zh: 其法，選人以居職，頒俸以養廉，去污濫以清政，勸農桑以富民。

translations.literal: The method was to select men to hold office, issue salaries to nurture integrity, remove corruption to clarify government, and encourage agriculture and sericulture to enrich the people.
translations.idiomatic: You chose capable men for office, paid salaries to encourage integrity, swept away corruption, and promoted farming and sericulture to enrich the people.

sentences.zh: 不及三年，號稱大治。

translations.literal: In less than three years they were acclaimed as greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years those regions were said to be well governed.

sentences.zh: 諸路之民望陛下之拯己，如赤子之求母。

translations.literal: The people of the various circuits look to Your Majesty to save them as an infant looks to its mother.
translations.idiomatic: The people of every circuit look to Your Majesty to save them as infants look to their mother.

sentences.zh: 先帝陟遐，國難並興，天開聖人，纘承大統，即用歷代遺制，內立省部，外設監司，自中統至今五六年間，外侮內叛繼繼不絕，然能使官離債負，民安賦役，府庫粗實，倉廩粗完，鈔法粗行，國用粗足，官吏遷轉，政事更新，皆陛下克保祖宗之基、信用先王之法所致。

translations.literal: The late Emperor ascended afar; national difficulties arose together; Heaven opened a sage who succeeded to the great succession and at once employed the surviving institutions of successive dynasties, establishing ministries within and supervisory commissioners without—from the Zhongtong era to the present, five or six years, foreign insults and internal rebellions have followed one after another without cease, yet he has been able to make officials leave debt, the people secure in levies and corvée, the treasuries roughly filled, the granaries roughly complete, paper currency roughly in circulation, state expenditures roughly sufficient, officials transferred in office, and government affairs renewed—all owing to Your Majesty's ability to preserve the foundation of the ancestors and trust the methods of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: After the late emperor's death troubles arose on every side, yet Heaven raised a sage to succeed to the throne. You at once adopted institutions handed down from earlier dynasties, establishing ministries at the center and supervisory commissioners in the provinces. For five or six years since the Zhongtong era, foreign attacks and internal rebellions have not ceased, yet officials are freed from debt, the people bear their taxes, treasuries and granaries are reasonably full, paper money circulates, state revenue is adequate, and government is renewed—all because Your Majesty has preserved the ancestral foundation and trusted the ways of the sage kings.

sentences.zh: 今創始治道，正宜上答天心，下結民心，睦親族以固本，建儲副以重祚，定大臣以當國，開經筵以格心，修邊備以防虞，蓄糧餉以待歉，立學校以育才，勸農桑以厚生。

translations.literal: Now, at the beginning of the way of governance, it is precisely fitting to answer Heaven's heart above and bind the people's hearts below: harmonize kin to solidify the root, establish the heir to weight the succession, fix great ministers to bear the state, open the classics lecture to rectify the heart, repair border defenses to guard against trouble, store grain and funds to await lean years, establish schools to nurture talent, and encourage agriculture and sericulture to thicken the people's livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as you begin the work of governance, you should answer Heaven above and win the people's hearts below: reconcile your kin to strengthen the throne, name an heir to secure the succession, appoint steadfast ministers to govern, hold lectures on the classics to refine your mind, strengthen the borders, store grain against famine, establish schools, and promote agriculture to enrich the people.

sentences.zh: 是可以光先烈，成帝德，遺子孫，流遠譽。

translations.literal: By this one can glorify the former emperors, complete imperial virtue, bequeath to descendants, and leave a far-reaching reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus you will honor your forebears, fulfill imperial virtue, secure your descendants, and win lasting renown.

sentences.zh: 以陛下才略，行此有餘。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's talent and strategy, to carry this out leaves a surplus of capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's ability is more than sufficient for all of this.

sentences.zh: 邇者伏聞聰聽日煩，朝廷政令日改月異，如木始栽而復移，屋既架而復毀。

translations.literal: Recently I have heard that Your Majesty's attention grows daily more burdened and court policies change day by day and month by month, like a tree just planted then moved again, or a house already framed then torn down.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately I hear that Your Majesty is overwhelmed with business and court orders change from day to day, like trees replanted as soon as they are set, or houses torn down as soon as they are framed.

sentences.zh: 遠近臣民不勝戰懼，惟恐大本一廢，遠業難成，為陛下之後憂，國家之重害。

translations.literal: Near and far, officials and people cannot bear their trembling fear, dreading only that once the great foundation is abandoned the distant enterprise will be hard to complete—this would be a later worry for Your Majesty and a grave harm to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people near and far tremble with fear lest the great foundation be lost and your long-term aims fail—a grave worry for Your Majesty and a heavy blow to the state.

sentences.zh: 帝怒為釋。

translations.literal: The Emperor's anger was released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger subsided.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜昭文館大學士，詳定禮儀事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for the Spread of Culture and charged with reviewing ritual matters in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made grand academician of the Hall for the Spread of Culture and assigned to revise ritual protocol.

sentences.zh: 其年，襄陽下，遂議取宋。

translations.literal: That year Xiangyang fell, and thereupon deliberation turned to taking Song.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Xiangyang fell, and the court began to discuss conquering Song.

sentences.zh: 樞奏如求大將，非右丞相安童、知樞密院伯顏不可。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized that if a great general were sought, none but Right Chancellor Antong and Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Bayan would do.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized that if a great commander were needed, only Right Chancellor Antong and Bayan, director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, would suffice.

sentences.zh: 十一年，樞言：「陛下降不殺人之詔。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Shu said: "Your Majesty has issued an edict forbidding killing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Shu said, "Your Majesty has issued an edict forbidding killing.

sentences.zh: 伯顏濟江，兵不逾時，西起蜀川，東薄海隅，降城三十，戶逾百萬，自古平南，未有如此之神捷者。

translations.literal: Bayan crossed the Yangzi; the army did not exceed its season—from Shu in the west to the sea's edge in the east, thirty cities surrendered and households exceeded a million; since antiquity in pacifying the south there has never been such divine swiftness.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan crossed the Yangzi and within a season swept from Sichuan in the west to the coast in the east. Thirty cities surrendered and more than a million households submitted—never in history had the south been conquered with such speed.

sentences.zh: 今自夏徂秋，一城不降，皆由軍官不思國之大計，不體陛下之深仁，利財剽殺所致。

translations.literal: Now from summer to autumn not a single city has surrendered—all because military officers do not consider the great plan of the state, do not embody Your Majesty's deep benevolence, and kill for profit and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from summer to autumn not one city has surrendered, because officers ignore the state's larger interest, disregard Your Majesty's deep humanity, and kill and plunder for profit.

sentences.zh: 揚州、焦山、淮安，人殊死戰，我雖克勝，所傷亦多。

translations.literal: At Yangzhou, Jiaoshan, and Huai'an the people fought to the death with exceptional fierceness; though we conquered, our losses were also many.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangzhou, Jiaoshan, and Huai'an the defenders fought to the last. Though we won, our casualties were heavy.

sentences.zh: 宋之不能為國審矣，而臨安未肯輕下，好生惡死，人之常情，蓋不敢也，惟懼吾招徠止殺之信不堅耳。

translations.literal: That Song can no longer sustain itself as a state is clear, yet Lin'an is unwilling to surrender lightly—loving life and hating death is the constant disposition of men; they probably do not dare, fearing only that our summons to come over and our pledge to halt killing are not firm.
translations.idiomatic: Song can no longer survive as a state, yet Lin'an will not surrender easily. Men naturally cling to life and fear death; they dare not submit because they do not trust our promise to spare them.

sentences.zh: 宜申止殺之詔，使賞罰必立，恩信必行，聖慮不勞，軍力不費矣。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to reiterate the edict halting killing, so that rewards and punishments are surely established, favor and trust surely practiced—then the sage's concern will not be labored and military strength will not be wasted."
translations.idiomatic: Reissue the order to halt killing, enforce rewards and punishments, and keep faith with promises—then Your Majesty need not strain yourself and the army need not be wasted."

sentences.zh: 又請禁宋鞭背、黥面及諸濫刑。

translations.literal: He also requested forbidding Song's flogging of the back, tattooing of the face, and all abusive punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Song's flogging, facial tattooing, and other abusive punishments be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 十三年，拜翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Hanlin academician recipient of edicts.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒，年七十八，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died, aged seventy-eight; his posthumous title was Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died at seventy-eight and was given the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 樞天質含弘而仁恕，恭敏而儉勤，未嘗疑人欺己。

translations.literal: Shu by nature was broad-minded, benevolent, and forgiving, respectful, keen, frugal, and diligent; he never suspected others of deceiving him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Shu was magnanimous, benevolent, and forgiving, respectful and diligent, frugal and tireless. He never suspected others of deceiving him.

sentences.zh: 有負其德，亦不留怨。

translations.literal: Even when someone failed in virtue toward him, he kept no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who wronged him found no lasting grudge in his heart.

sentences.zh: 憂患之來，不見言色。

translations.literal: When trouble came, it did not show in his words or countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble came, it never showed in his speech or expression.

sentences.zh: 有來即謀，必反復告之。

translations.literal: When someone came to consult him, he always advised repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever came to consult him received careful, repeated counsel.

sentences.zh: 子煒，仕為平章政事；

translations.literal: His son Wei served as Grand Councillor;
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei rose to grand councillor;

sentences.zh: 從子燧，官至翰林學士承旨，以文章大家知名，卒諡曰文。

translations.literal: his nephew Sui reached the post of Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, was renowned as a great master of letters, and upon death received the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: his nephew Sui became Hanlin academician recipient of edicts, won fame as a master of prose, and at death received the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: ○許衡

translations.literal: ○ Xu Heng
translations.idiomatic: ○ Xu Heng

sentences.zh: 許衡，字仲平，懷之河內人也，世為農。

translations.literal: Xu Heng, courtesy name Zhongping, was a native of Henei in Huai; his family for generations were farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Heng, whose courtesy name was Zhongping, came from Henei in Huai. His family had been farmers for generations.

sentences.zh: 父通，避地河南，以泰和九年九月生衡於新鄭縣。

translations.literal: His father was Tong. Taking refuge in Henan, in the ninth month of the ninth year of the Taihe era he bore Heng in Xinzheng County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong fled south to Henan; in the ninth month of the ninth year of the Taihe reign (1216), Xu Heng was born in Xinzheng County.

sentences.zh: 幼有異質，七歲入學，授章句，問其師曰：「讀書何為？」

translations.literal: As a child he had an uncommon nature. At seven he entered school and was taught chapter-and-sentence reading; he asked his teacher, "What is reading books for?"
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he showed unusual gifts. At seven he began school and was taught the classics clause by clause. He asked his teacher, "What is the purpose of reading?"

sentences.zh: 師曰：「取​​科第耳！」

translations.literal: The teacher said, "To win an examination degree, that is all!"
translations.idiomatic: His teacher replied, "To pass the examinations and win office—that's all."

sentences.zh: 曰：「如斯而已乎？」

translations.literal: He said, "Is that all there is to it?"
translations.idiomatic: Is that all?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 師大奇之。

translations.literal: The teacher was greatly astonished at him.
translations.idiomatic: The teacher was astonished.

sentences.zh: 每授書，又能問其旨義。

translations.literal: Each time books were taught, he could also inquire into their essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was taught a text, he would also question its deeper meaning.

sentences.zh: 久之，師謂其父母曰：「兒穎悟不凡，他日必有大過人者，吾非其師也。」

translations.literal: After some time, the teacher said to his parents, "The boy is unusually quick and perceptive; someday he will greatly surpass others. I am not his teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the teacher told his parents, "Your son is exceptionally bright. One day he will far surpass ordinary men. I am not qualified to be his teacher."

sentences.zh: 遂辭去，父母強之不能止。

translations.literal: He thereupon took leave and departed; his parents urged him strongly but could not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned anyway; his parents tried to keep him but could not.

sentences.zh: 如是者凡更三師。

translations.literal: In this way he changed teachers three times in all.
translations.idiomatic: In all he went through three teachers in this fashion.

sentences.zh: 稍長，嗜學如飢渴，然遭世亂，且貧無書。

translations.literal: When he had grown somewhat, he loved learning as one loves food and drink in hunger and thirst; yet he encountered turmoil in the age, and was moreover poor and without books.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he hungered for learning, but the times were chaotic and he was too poor to own books.

sentences.zh: 嘗從日者家見《書》疏義，因請寓宿，手抄歸。

translations.literal: Once at a fortune-teller's house he saw a commentary on the Book of Documents; he therefore asked to lodge there overnight and copied it by hand to take home.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a diviner's home he came upon a commentary on the Book of Documents. He asked to stay the night and copied the text by hand to take home.

sentences.zh: 既逃難徂徠山，始得《易》王輔嗣說。

translations.literal: After escaping the troubles to Mount Cula, he first obtained Wang Fuzhi's commentary on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: After fleeing to Mount Culai he obtained Wang Bi's commentary on the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 時兵亂中，衡夜思晝誦，身體而力踐之，言動必揆諸義而後發。

translations.literal: Amid the military turmoil of the time, Heng pondered by night and recited by day, embodied it in the body and vigorously put it into practice; in speech and action he invariably measured against righteousness before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the wars Heng studied by night and recited by day, striving to live what he learned. He never spoke or acted without first weighing it against moral principle.

sentences.zh: 嘗暑中過河陽，渴甚，道有梨，眾爭取噉之，衡獨危坐樹下自若。

translations.literal: Once in midsummer he passed through Heyang; extremely thirsty, there were pears by the road; the crowd scrambled to take and eat them, but Heng alone sat upright beneath a tree, composed as if nothing were the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Once in midsummer, passing through Heyang desperately thirsty, he found pears by the road. Everyone snatched them up to eat, but Heng alone sat calmly under a tree, unmoved.

sentences.zh: 或問之，曰：「非其有而取之，不可也。」

translations.literal: Someone asked him; he said, "What is not one's own—to take it is not permissible."
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, he said, "One must not take what does not belong to oneself."

sentences.zh: 人曰：「世亂，此無主。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "The age is in turmoil; these have no owner."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "These are troubled times—the pears have no owner."

sentences.zh: 曰：「梨無主，吾心獨無主乎？」

translations.literal: He said, "The pears have no owner—does my heart alone have no master?"
translations.idiomatic: The pears may have no owner," he replied, "but does my heart have no master?"

sentences.zh: 轉魯留魏，人見其有德，稍稍從之。

translations.literal: He moved to Lu and stayed in Wei; people saw that he possessed virtue and gradually followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Lu and settled in Wei. Seeing his character, people gradually gathered around him.

sentences.zh: 居三年，聞亂且定，乃還懷。

translations.literal: After dwelling three years, hearing that turmoil was about to settle, he then returned to Huai.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, hearing that peace was returning, he went back to Huai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 往來河、洛間，從柳城姚樞得伊洛程氏及新安硃氏書，益大有得。

translations.literal: Traveling to and fro between the Yellow and Luo rivers, from Yao Shu of Liucheng he obtained the books of the Cheng family of Luoyang and the Zhu family of Xin'an, and gained still more greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling between the Yellow and Luo rivers, he obtained from Yao Shu of Liucheng the works of the Cheng brothers of Luoyang and the Zhu family of Xin'an, and made great progress.

sentences.zh: 尋居蘇門，與樞及竇默相講習。

translations.literal: Soon he dwelt at Sumen, and with Shu and Dou Mo mutually lectured and studied together.
translations.idiomatic: He soon settled at Sumen, where he studied together with Yao Shu and Dou Mo.

sentences.zh: 凡經傳、子史、禮樂、名物、星曆、兵刑、食貨、水利之類，無所不講，而慨然以道為己任。

translations.literal: As for the classics and commentaries, masters and histories, rites and music, nomenclature, astronomy and calendrics, military affairs and punishments, grain and goods, waterworks, and the like—there was nothing he did not discuss, and he sighed with resolve to take the Way as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on everything from the classics, histories, rites, music, nomenclature, astronomy, military law, finance, and irrigation to water control, and resolutely took the Way as his personal mission.

sentences.zh: 嘗語人曰：「綱常不可一日而亡於天下，苟在上者無以任之，則在下之任也。」

translations.literal: Once he said to people, "The constants of ethics cannot for a single day perish in the world; if those above have no means to uphold them, then it is the charge of those below."
translations.idiomatic: He once told others, "The moral order cannot vanish from the world even for a day. If those in power will not uphold it, then those below must bear the responsibility."

sentences.zh: 凡喪祭娶嫁，必徵於禮，以倡其鄉人，學者浸盛。

translations.literal: For all funerals, sacrifices, marriages, and betrothals he invariably consulted the rites, taking the lead for the people of his village; scholars gradually increased in number.
translations.idiomatic: For every funeral, sacrifice, marriage, or betrothal he observed the rites strictly and set an example for his neighbors, and the number of his students steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 家貧躬耕，粟熟則食，粟不熟則食糠核菜茹，處之泰然，謳誦之聲聞戶外如金石。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he personally plowed the fields. When grain ripened he ate it; when grain did not ripen he ate chaff, pits, and greens—he bore it with calm composure, and the sound of his chanting and recitation beyond the door was like metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor he farmed his own land. In good years he ate grain; in bad years he ate chaff, pits, and wild greens—all with equanimity. The sound of his chanting drifted outside his door clear as bell and chime.

sentences.zh: 財有餘，即以分諸族人及諸生之貧者。

translations.literal: When he had surplus wealth, he immediately distributed it among clansmen and poor students.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had money to spare, he gave it to needy clansmen and impoverished students.

sentences.zh: 人有所遺，一毫弗義，弗受也。

translations.literal: When people offered him gifts, not one cash that was not righteous did he accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every gift that was not strictly righteous—not a single cash would he take.

sentences.zh: 樞嘗被召入京師，以其雪齋居衡，命守者館之，衡拒不受。

translations.literal: Once Shu was summoned to the capital; he had his Snow Studio for Heng to live in and ordered the caretaker to lodge him, but Heng refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Shu was summoned to the capital, he offered Heng his Snow Studio and told the caretaker to host him, but Heng refused.

sentences.zh: 庭有果熟爛墮地，童子過之，亦不睨視而去，其家人化之如此。

translations.literal: In the courtyard fruit ripened and rotted and fell to the ground; passing boys would not even glance at it before going away—his household was transformed to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: When fruit ripened and fell rotting in the courtyard, children passing by never even glanced at it. His whole household had been transformed to this degree.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，世祖出王秦中，以姚樞為勸農使，教民畊植。

translations.literal: In jiayin, the Founder went out to be king in Qinzhong; he appointed Yao Shu Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture to teach the people to plow and plant.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiayin year (1254), Kublai went to govern Qinzhong. He made Yao Shu commissioner for encouraging agriculture and charged him with teaching the people to farm.

sentences.zh: 又思所以化秦人，乃召衡為京兆提學。

translations.literal: He also thought how to transform the people of Qin, and therefore summoned Heng as Metropolitan Commissioner for the Promotion of Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking also to civilize the people of Qin, he summoned Xu Heng as metropolitan commissioner for the promotion of learning.

sentences.zh: 秦人新脫於兵，欲學無師，聞衡來，人人莫不喜幸來學。

translations.literal: The people of Qin had newly escaped from warfare; they wished to learn but had no teachers; hearing Heng was coming, there was not one who did not rejoice and come gladly to study.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qin had only recently emerged from war. They wanted to learn but had no teachers. When word came that Xu Heng was coming, everyone rejoiced and flocked to study with him.

sentences.zh: 郡縣皆建學校，民大化之。

translations.literal: Every commandery and county established schools; the people were greatly transformed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Schools were established in every commandery and county, and the people were greatly transformed.

sentences.zh: 世祖南征，乃還懷，學者攀留之不得，從送之臨潼而歸。

translations.literal: When the Founder marched south on campaign, he then returned to Huai; scholars clung to him and could not keep him; they followed and escorted him to Lintong and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai marched south on campaign, Heng returned to Huai. Students tried to detain him but could not; they followed him as far as Lintong and then went home.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，世祖即皇帝位，召至京師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, the Founder ascended the imperial throne; he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong (1260), when Kublai took the throne, Xu Heng was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時王文統以言利進為平章政事，衡、樞輩入侍，言治亂休戚，必以義為本。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Wentshi, having advanced through speaking of profit, became Grand Councillor; Heng, Shu, and the like entered to attend, and in speaking of order and disorder, weal and woe, they invariably took righteousness as the root.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wentshi had risen to grand councillor by advocating profit. Xu Heng, Yao Shu, and their circle attended the court and, whenever they spoke of governance or the state's fortunes, always placed moral principle first.

sentences.zh: 文統患之。

translations.literal: Wentshi was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Wentshi resented this.

sentences.zh: 且竇默日於帝前排其學術，疑衡與之為表裡，乃奏以樞為太子太師，默為太子太傅，衡為太子太保，陽為尊用之，實不使數侍上也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Dou Mo daily before the emperor criticized his learning; he suspected Heng and Mo were acting in concert inside and out, and therefore memorialized to appoint Shu as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Mo as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Heng as Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent—outwardly honoring and employing them, but in fact not allowing them frequently to attend the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Mo also criticized Wentshi's scholarship daily before the emperor. Suspecting collusion between Heng and Mo, Wentshi memorialized the throne to appoint Yao Shu grand preceptor, Dou Mo grand tutor, and Xu Heng grand protector of the heir apparent—ostensibly honoring them, but in fact keeping them from frequent access to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 默以屢攻文統不中，欲因東宮以避禍，與樞拜命，將入謝。

translations.literal: Mo, because his repeated attacks on Wentshi had not succeeded, wished to rely on the Eastern Palace to avoid calamity; he and Shu accepted the appointments and were about to enter to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Mo, having failed repeatedly to bring down Wentshi, hoped the Eastern Palace appointment would offer refuge from trouble. He and Yao Shu accepted the posts and were about to enter court to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 衡曰：「此不安於義也，姑勿論。

translations.literal: Heng said, "This is not secure in righteousness; for the moment do not discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Heng said, "Setting that aside as a matter of principle, consider this:

sentences.zh: 禮，師傅與太子位東西鄉，師傅坐，太子乃坐。

translations.literal: According to ritual, tutor and preceptor and the Heir Apparent face east and west; the tutor and preceptor sit, and only then does the Heir Apparent sit.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, tutors sit facing the heir across the hall, and only after they are seated may the heir take his seat.

sentences.zh: 公等度能復此乎？

translations.literal: Do you gentlemen reckon you can restore this?
translations.idiomatic: Can you truly restore that practice?

sentences.zh: 不能，則師道自我廢也。」

translations.literal: If not, then the Way of the teacher will be abolished by us ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: If not, we ourselves will be the ones to destroy the teacher's proper station."

sentences.zh: 樞以為然，乃相與懷制立殿下，五辭乃免。

translations.literal: Shu thought this correct; they thereupon together, grasping their credentials, stood below the hall, declined five times, and were released from the appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shu agreed. Together they stood below the hall holding their credentials and declined five times before they were excused.

sentences.zh: 改命樞大司農，默翰林侍講學士，衡國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Their appointments were changed: Shu became Grand Minister of Agriculture, Mo Hanlin Academician Explaining the Classics, and Heng Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: They were reassigned instead: Yao Shu as grand minister of agriculture, Dou Mo as Hanlin lecturing academician, and Xu Heng as director of the National University.

sentences.zh: 未幾，衡亦謝病歸。

translations.literal: Before long, Heng also requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xu Heng also resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，帝以安童為右丞相，欲衡輔之，復召至京師，命議事中書省。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, the emperor made Antong Right Grand Councillor and wished Heng to assist him; he again summoned Heng to the capital and ordered him to deliberative affairs of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiyuan (1265), the emperor appointed Antong right grand councillor and wanted Xu Heng to assist him. Heng was summoned again to the capital and ordered to take part in Secretariat deliberations.

sentences.zh: 衡乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Heng thereupon submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xu Heng thereupon submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣性識愚陋，學術荒疏，不意虛名，偶塵聖聽。

translations.literal: Your servant's nature and understanding are dull and crude, his learning barren and sparse; I did not expect hollow renown, yet by chance have sullied the sacred ear.
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant's nature is dull and my learning shallow. I never expected such empty renown, yet by chance my name has reached Your Majesty's ears."

sentences.zh: 陛下好賢樂善，舍短取長，雖以臣之不才，自甲寅至今十有三年，凡八被詔旨，中懷自念，何以報塞。

translations.literal: Your Majesty loves the worthy and delights in goodness, setting aside shortcomings and taking what is long; though your servant is without talent, from jiayin until now thirteen years have passed; eight times in all have I received imperial edicts; within my breast I reflect—with what can I repay and fulfill?
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty loves the worthy and delights in virtue, setting aside faults and drawing on strengths. Though I am without talent, from the jiayin year until now—thirteen years—I have received eight imperial summonses. I ask myself constantly how I can ever repay such grace."

sentences.zh: 又日者面奉德音，叮嚀懇至，中書大務，容臣盡言。

translations.literal: Moreover, recently in audience I received your virtuous words, earnestly repeated and utmost in sincerity; as to the great affairs of the Secretariat, you allowed your servant to speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: "Recently in audience Your Majesty spoke with earnest concern and allowed me to speak freely on the great affairs of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 臣雖昏愚，荷陛下知待如此其厚，敢不罄竭所有，裨益萬分。

translations.literal: Your servant, though muddled and foolish, has received Your Majesty's knowledge and treatment so very generous—how dare I not exhaust all I possess, to benefit even one ten-thousandth part?
translations.idiomatic: "Though I am dull-witted, I have received such generous trust from Your Majesty. How dare I not give all I have, however small the benefit?"

sentences.zh: 孟子以「責難於君謂之恭，陳善閉邪謂之敬」；

translations.literal: Mencius held that "to hold difficulty before the ruler is called respect; to set forth goodness and shut out what is perverse is called reverence";
translations.idiomatic: "Mencius said that to hold one's ruler to high standards is respect, and to offer good counsel while blocking what is corrupt is reverence;"

sentences.zh: 孔子謂「以道事君，不可則止」。

translations.literal: Confucius said, "To serve the ruler by the Way—if it is not possible, then stop."
translations.idiomatic: "Confucius said that to serve one's ruler by the Way, and to withdraw when that proves impossible."

sentences.zh: 臣之所守，大意蓋如此也。

translations.literal: What your servant upholds, in its general purport, is roughly thus.
translations.idiomatic: "That, in broad outline, is the principle by which I mean to conduct myself."

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下寬其不佞，察其至懷，則區區之愚，亦或有小補云。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself and hope Your Majesty will pardon my lack of cleverness and discern my utmost sincerity—then this petty foolishness may also offer some small benefit.
translations.idiomatic: "I beg Your Majesty to forgive my lack of wit and discern my sincere intent; then this humble counsel may perhaps prove of some small use."

sentences.zh: 其一曰：自古立國，皆有規模。

translations.literal: The first point says: From antiquity in establishing a state, all have had a model and scale.
translations.idiomatic: "First: every state founded since antiquity has had its institutional framework."

sentences.zh: 循而行之，則治功可期。

translations.literal: If one follows and carries it out, then the achievement of order can be expected.
translations.idiomatic: "Follow it consistently, and good governance can be achieved."

sentences.zh: 否則心疑目眩，變易分更，未見其可也。

translations.literal: Otherwise the mind is doubtful and the eyes dazzled, changes and divisions multiply—one does not see how it can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: "Otherwise the ruler grows uncertain, policy shifts constantly, and success becomes impossible."

sentences.zh: 昔子產相衰周之列國，孔明治西蜀之一隅，且有定論，終身由之；

translations.literal: Formerly Zichan served as minister to the feudal states of the declining Zhou; Kongming governed a single corner of western Shu—yet even they had fixed conclusions and followed them all their lives;
translations.idiomatic: "Even Zichan, minister to the waning Zhou states, and Kongming, who governed only a corner of western Shu, held to fixed principles for life;"

sentences.zh: 而堂堂天下，可無一定之說而妄為之哉？

translations.literal: Yet for the vast realm under heaven, can there be no fixed doctrine and rash action?
translations.idiomatic: "how much more so for a great empire—can we act without a settled policy?"

sentences.zh: 考之前代，北方之有中夏者，必行漢法乃可長久。

translations.literal: Examining previous ages, those from the north who possessed the Central Plains had to execute Han law before they could endure long.
translations.idiomatic: "History shows that every northern dynasty that ruled the Central Plains endured only by adopting Han institutions."

sentences.zh: 故後魏、遼、金歷年最多，他不能者，皆亂亡相繼，史冊具載，昭然可考。

translations.literal: Therefore Later Wei, Liao, and Jin lasted the most years; those who could not do so all saw disorder and destruction follow in succession—the historical records fully set this forth, clear and verifiable.
translations.idiomatic: "The Northern Wei, Liao, and Jin lasted longest for this reason; those that did not follow this path fell one after another—the histories record it plainly."

sentences.zh: 使國家而居朔漠，則無事論此也。

translations.literal: If the state dwelt in the northern deserts, then there would be no need to discuss this.
translations.idiomatic: "Had the dynasty remained on the northern steppe, this question would not arise."

sentences.zh: 今日之治，非此奚宜？

translations.literal: For governance today, if not this, what is fitting?
translations.idiomatic: "But for governing today, what course is more fitting?"

sentences.zh: 夫陸行宜車，水行宜舟，反之則不能行；

translations.literal: For travel on land, carts are fitting; for travel on water, boats are fitting—reversed, one cannot proceed.
translations.idiomatic: "On land one travels by cart; on water by boat—reverse that and you cannot move."

sentences.zh: 幽燕食寒，蜀漢食熱，反之則必有變。

translations.literal: In Youyan one eats according to cold; in Shu and Han one eats according to heat—reversed, there must be alteration.
translations.idiomatic: "In the cold north one eats warming foods; in hot Shu one eats cooling foods—do the reverse and illness follows."

sentences.zh: 以是論之，國家之當行漢法無疑也。

translations.literal: By this reasoning, that the state ought to execute Han law is without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: "By the same logic, there can be no doubt that the dynasty ought to adopt Han law."

sentences.zh: 然萬世國俗，累朝勳舊，一旦驅之下從臣僕之謀，改就亡國之俗，其勢有甚難者。

translations.literal: Yet the custom of the realm for myriad generations, meritorious old families of successive courts—to drive them at once to follow the plotting of subject and servant, changing to the customs of perished states—the momentum presents great difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet the Mongols have their ancient customs, and families meritorious under successive reigns cannot overnight be forced, at the urging of servile advisors, to adopt the customs of doomed states. The difficulty is immense."

sentences.zh: 竊嘗思之，寒之與暑，固為不同。

translations.literal: I have privately often reflected on this: cold and heat are indeed different.
translations.idiomatic: "I have often reflected: cold and heat are certainly different."

sentences.zh: 然寒之變暑也，始於微溫，溫而熱，熱而暑，積百有八十二日而寒始盡。

translations.literal: Yet when cold changes to heat, it begins with slight warmth; warmth becomes heat, heat becomes swelter—accumulating one hundred and eighty-two days before cold is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet cold turns to heat only gradually—from slight warmth to warmth, then heat, then sweltering summer—a hundred and eighty-two days before winter's chill is fully gone."

sentences.zh: 暑之變寒，其勢亦然，是亦積之之驗也。

translations.literal: Heat's change to cold—its momentum is likewise; this too is proof of accumulated transformation.
translations.idiomatic: "The change from heat back to cold follows the same pattern—proof that transformation requires accumulation over time."

sentences.zh: 苟能漸之摩之，待以歲月，心堅而確，事易而常，未有不可變者。

translations.literal: If one can gradually advance and polish it, waiting with months and years—the mind firm and sure, affairs easy and constant—there has never been what cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: "If change comes gradually, patiently, over years—with steadfast purpose and steady application—nothing is ultimately unchangeable."

sentences.zh: 此在陛下尊信而堅守之，不雜小人，不責近效，不恤流言，則致治之功，庶幾可成矣。

translations.literal: This depends on Your Majesty honoring and trusting it and firmly holding to it—not mixing in petty men, not demanding immediate results, not heeding idle talk—then the achievement of bringing order may perhaps be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: "This requires Your Majesty to honor the policy, hold firm, keep petty men at a distance, demand no instant results, and pay no heed to gossip—then the work of bringing order may succeed."

sentences.zh: 二曰：中書之務不勝其煩，然其大要在用人、立法二者而已矣。

translations.literal: Second: the affairs of the Secretariat cannot bear their own vexation, yet their great essentials lie in only two things—employing men and establishing law.
translations.idiomatic: "Second: the Secretariat's business is endlessly complex, but its essentials are only two: selecting personnel and establishing law."

sentences.zh: 近而譬之：發之在首，不以手理而以櫛理；

translations.literal: Taking a nearby analogy: hair on the head is not combed with the hand but with a comb;
translations.idiomatic: "To put it plainly: hair on the head is combed not with the fingers but with a comb;"

sentences.zh: 食之在器，不以手取而以匕取。

translations.literal: food in a vessel is not taken with the hand but with a spoon.
translations.idiomatic: "food in a bowl is eaten not with the hand but with a spoon."

sentences.zh: 手雖不能，而用櫛與匕，是即手之為也。

translations.literal: Though the hand cannot do it, yet using comb and spoon—this is what the hand accomplishes.
translations.idiomatic: "The hand alone cannot manage these tasks; yet through comb and spoon it still achieves its purpose."

sentences.zh: 上之用人，何以異此。

translations.literal: The sovereign's employment of men—how does it differ from this?
translations.idiomatic: "So too in employing men—what difference is there?"

sentences.zh: 然人之賢否，未知其詳，固不可得而遽用也。

translations.literal: Yet whether a person is worthy or not, not knowing the particulars, one naturally cannot hastily employ him.
translations.idiomatic: "One cannot know at once who is worthy and who is not, so hasty appointment is impossible."

sentences.zh: 然或已知其孰為君子，孰為小人，而復患得患失，莫敢進退，徒曰知人，而實不能用人，亦何益哉！

translations.literal: Yet sometimes one already knows who is the noble man and who is the petty man, yet again fears gain and fears loss, daring neither advance nor retreat—vainly saying one knows men, while in fact unable to employ men—what benefit is there!
translations.idiomatic: "Yet even when one knows who is honorable and who is base, to waver in fear of gain and loss, daring neither to promote nor dismiss, is to claim knowledge of men while in fact refusing to use them—of what use is that?"

sentences.zh: 人莫不飲食也，獨膳夫為能調五味之和；

translations.literal: Among people, none do not eat and drink; only the cook can harmonize the five flavors;
translations.idiomatic: "Everyone eats, but only a cook can blend the five flavors;"

sentences.zh: 莫不睹日月也，獨星官為能步虧食之數者，誠以得其法故也。

translations.literal: none fail to see sun and moon; only the astronomer can pace the numbers of eclipse and deficiency—truly because he obtains the method.
translations.idiomatic: "everyone sees the sun and moon, but only an astronomer can calculate eclipses—because he possesses the proper method."

sentences.zh: 古人有言曰：「為高必因丘陵，為下必因川澤，為政必因先王之道。」

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: "To build high one must rely on hills and mounds; to build low one must rely on rivers and marshes; to govern one must rely on the Way of the former kings."
translations.idiomatic: "The ancients said: 'To build high one must start from hills; to dig deep one must follow rivers; to govern one must follow the way of the former kings.'"

sentences.zh: 今里巷之談，動以古為詬戲，不知今日口之所食，身之所衣，皆古人遺法而不可違者，豈天下之大，國家之重，而古之成法反可違邪？

translations.literal: Today talk in lanes and alleys readily takes antiquity as an object of mockery; they do not know that what today's mouths eat and bodies clothe themselves with are all methods left by the ancients and cannot be violated—can it be that for the vastness of the realm and the weight of the state, the accomplished laws of antiquity may on the contrary be violated?
translations.idiomatic: Yet street talk mocks the ancients, forgetting that the food we eat and clothes we wear are all methods handed down from antiquity and cannot be disregarded. Can the laws that govern an empire be treated with less respect?"

sentences.zh: 其亦弗思甚矣！

translations.literal: This too is extreme failure to think!
translations.idiomatic: "That is blindness indeed!"

sentences.zh: 夫治人者法也，守法者人也。

translations.literal: Those who govern men are law; those who uphold law are men.
translations.idiomatic: "Law governs men; men uphold law."

sentences.zh: 人法相維，上安下順，而宰執優游於廊廟之上，不煩不勞，此所謂省也。

translations.literal: Men and law mutually sustain each other; above is secure, below is compliant, and chief ministers move at ease above the court hall—unvexed, untiring—this is what is called efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: "When men and law support each other, superiors are secure and subordinates obedient, and ministers govern at ease from the palace halls without strain or exhaustion—that is true efficiency."

sentences.zh: 夫立法用人，今雖未能遽如古昔，然已仕者當給俸以養其廉，未仕者當寬立條格，俾就敘用，則失職之怨少可舒矣。

translations.literal: As for establishing law and employing men—today though one cannot hastily be like ancient times, yet those already in office ought to be given salaries to nurture their integrity; those not yet in office ought to be broadly given regulations and standards, enabling them to proceed to ordered employment—then the resentment of those who lost office can somewhat be eased.
translations.idiomatic: "Though we cannot immediately restore ancient practice in legislation and appointments, officials in post should receive salaries sufficient to sustain their integrity, and standards should be broadened so that the unemployed may enter service in orderly fashion—thus easing resentment among those passed over."

sentences.zh: 外設監司以察污濫，內專吏部以定資歷，則非分之求漸可息矣。

translations.literal: Externally establish supervisory commissioners to inspect corruption and abuse; internally concentrate the Ministry of Personnel to fix seniority and credentials—then improper demands can gradually cease.
translations.idiomatic: "Establish external inspectors to curb corruption, and concentrate authority in the Ministry of Personnel to fix ranks and seniority—then improper demands will gradually cease."

sentences.zh: 再任三任，抑高舉下，則人才爵位略可平矣。

translations.literal: Two terms, three terms—restrain the high and raise the low—then talent and rank and office can roughly be leveled.
translations.idiomatic: "Limit consecutive terms, restrain the over-promoted and elevate the deserving—then talent and rank may come into rough balance."

sentences.zh: 至於貴家之世襲，品官之任子，版籍之數，續當議之，亦不可緩也。

translations.literal: As for hereditary succession in noble houses, office-holders' appointment of sons, the numbers of registry rolls—these should continue to be deliberated and cannot be delayed either.
translations.idiomatic: "Questions of hereditary privilege among noble families, sons succeeding fathers in office, and registry rolls all remain to be addressed—and cannot be postponed."

sentences.zh: 其三曰：民生有欲，無主乃亂，上天眷命，作之君師，此蓋以至難任之，非予之可安之地而娛之也。

translations.literal: The third point says: the people's livelihood has desires; without a lord there is disorder; Heaven in its favoring mandate made for them ruler and teacher—this is roughly charged as the most difficult task; it is not a place where one may rest at ease and take pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: "Third: the people have desires; without a ruler chaos ensues. Heaven in its grace appoints rulers and teachers to bear the hardest charge—not a post for ease and amusement."

sentences.zh: 是以堯、舜以來，聖帝明王，莫不兢兢業業、小心畏慎者，誠知天之所畀至難之任，初不可以易心處之也。

translations.literal: Therefore from Yao and Shun onward, sage emperors and enlightened kings—none failed to be cautious and reverent, treading carefully in fear—truly knowing that what Heaven bestows is the most difficult charge, which from the first cannot be met with an easy mind.
translations.idiomatic: "From Yao and Shun onward, every sage ruler has been cautious and reverent, knowing that Heaven's charge is supremely difficult and cannot be treated lightly."

sentences.zh: 知其為難而以難處，則難或可為；

translations.literal: Knowing it is difficult and meeting it with difficulty—then difficulty may perhaps be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: "Recognize the difficulty and meet it as difficulty, and the difficult may yet be done;"

sentences.zh: 不知為難而以易處，則他日之難有不可為者矣。

translations.literal: Not knowing it is difficult and meeting it with ease—then difficulties of later days will have what cannot be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: "treat it lightly, and future difficulties will prove impossible."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「為君難，為臣不易。」

translations.literal: Confucius said, "To be ruler is difficult; to be minister is not easy."
translations.idiomatic: "Confucius said, 'To be a ruler is hard; to be a minister is no easy matter.'"

sentences.zh: 為臣之道，臣已告之安童矣。

translations.literal: The Way of the minister—your servant has already told Antong of it.
translations.idiomatic: I have already explained the minister's duty to Antong."

sentences.zh: 至為君之難，尤陛下所當專意也。

translations.literal: As for the difficulty of being ruler—this especially is what Your Majesty ought to focus on wholeheartedly.
translations.idiomatic: "But the difficulty of ruling is what Your Majesty above all must keep in mind."

sentences.zh: 臣請言其切而要者：

translations.literal: Your servant requests to speak of what is pressing and essential:
translations.idiomatic: "Permit me to speak of what is most urgent and essential:"

sentences.zh: 夫人君不患出言之難，而患踐言之難。

translations.literal: For a ruler, the worry is not the difficulty of issuing words, but the difficulty of carrying them out.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's worry is not speaking rightly but doing what he has said.

sentences.zh: 知踐言之難，則其出言不容不慎矣。

translations.literal: Knowing the difficulty of carrying out words, one's issued words cannot but be careful.
translations.idiomatic: Once one knows how hard it is to keep one's word, one cannot speak carelessly.

sentences.zh: 昔劉安世行一不妄語，七年而後成。

translations.literal: In former times Liu Anshi practiced the single rule of not speaking rashly; seven years passed before he accomplished it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Anshi once vowed never to speak rashly; seven years passed before he mastered that single discipline.

sentences.zh: 夫安世一士人也，所交者一家之親、一鄉之眾也，同列之臣不過數十百人而止耳，而言猶若此，況天下之大，兆民之眾，事有萬變，日有萬機，人君以一身一心而酬酢之，欲言之無失，豈易能哉？

translations.literal: Now Anshi was a mere scholar; those he interacted with were kin of one household and folk of one village; colleagues were no more than several tens or hundreds; yet speech was still thus—how much more under the vastness of all under Heaven, the multitude of the myriad people, affairs changing in ten thousand ways, ten thousand matters daily? The ruler with one body and one mind must respond to them all; to wish that speech never err—how could that be easy?
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was only a private gentleman, mingling with one family's kin and one village's neighbors, answering to a few dozen colleagues at most—yet even for him speech was so hard. How much harder for a ruler who must answer, alone, to an empire of millions, with affairs shifting daily in endless variety? To speak without ever missing the mark is scarcely possible.

sentences.zh: 故有昔之所言而今日忘之者，今之所命而後日自違者，可否異同，紛更變易，紀綱不得布，法度不得立，臣下無所持循，奸人因以為弊，天下之人疑惑驚眩，且議其無法無信一至於此也。

translations.literal: Thus there are words spoken yesterday forgotten today; commands issued today violated tomorrow on one's own part; approval and disapproval differing, ceaselessly changing and altering; the framework cannot be laid out, laws and standards cannot be established; ministers below have nothing to hold to and follow; the crafty thereby create abuses; people under Heaven are confused, startled, and dazzled, and discuss that lack of law and trust has reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Hence words forgotten overnight, orders contradicted the next day, policies reversed and reversed again: the state's framework cannot hold, law cannot take root, and ministers have no fixed rule to follow. Crafty men exploit the chaos, while the people stagger in confusion and conclude that the throne has lost both law and trust.

sentences.zh: 此無他，至難之地不以難處，而以易處故也。

translations.literal: This has no other cause: in the most difficult place one does not meet difficulty with difficulty, but meets it with ease.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is simple: one faces the hardest duties with too easy a mind.

sentences.zh: 苟從《大學》之道，以修身為本，凡一言一動，必求其然與其所當然，不牽於愛，不蔽於憎，不因於喜，不激於怒，虛心端意，熟思而審處之，雖有不中者蓋鮮矣。

translations.literal: If one follows the Way of the Great Learning, taking self-cultivation as the root—for every word and every act one must seek what is so and what ought to be so, not drawn by affection, not blinded by hatred, not carried away by joy, not stirred by anger, with humble mind and upright intent, pondering deeply and judging carefully—though there be misses, they would surely be rare.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the Great Learning: make self-cultivation the root. Let every word and deed seek what is true and what is right—not swayed by love or hate, joy or anger. With an open mind and steady purpose, think long and judge carefully, and error will be rare.

sentences.zh: 奈何為人上者多樂舒肆，為人臣者多事容悅。

translations.literal: Alas, those above as rulers mostly delight in ease and license; those below as ministers mostly engage in ingratiating flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rulers too often indulge themselves, while ministers too often trade in flattery.

sentences.zh: 容悅本為私也，私心盛則不畏人矣；

translations.literal: Ingratiating flattery is rooted in private interest; when private interest flourishes, one does not fear others.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery springs from private interest; when self-interest flourishes, one no longer fears others.

sentences.zh: 舒肆本為欲也，欲心盛則不畏天矣。

translations.literal: Ease and license are rooted in desire; when desire flourishes, one does not fear Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Indulgence springs from appetite; when appetite flourishes, one no longer fears Heaven.

sentences.zh: 以不畏天之心，與不畏人之心，感合無間，則其所務者皆快心事耳。

translations.literal: With a heart that does not fear Heaven joined without interval to a heart that does not fear others, what one pursues are all matters of pleasing the heart alone.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven-fearing and people-fearing gone, heart and habit merge, and all that is pursued becomes mere self-indulgence.

sentences.zh: 快心則口慾言而言，身欲動而動，又安肯兢兢業業，以修身為本，一言一動，熟思而審處之乎？
