translations.literal: When the heart is pleased, the mouth desires to speak and speaks; the body desires to move and moves—how then would one be cautious and reverent, taking self-cultivation as root, pondering and judging every word and act?
translations.idiomatic: When pleasure leads, the mouth speaks as it wishes and the body moves as it wishes. Who then will be careful, root every act in self-cultivation, and weigh each word before it is uttered?

sentences.zh: 此人君踐言之難，而又難於天下之人也。

translations.literal: This is the difficulty for a ruler in carrying out his words—and what is difficult for him is difficult for all under Heaven as well.
translations.idiomatic: This is why a ruler's words are so hard to honor—and why the whole realm suffers when they are not.

sentences.zh: 人之情偽，有易有險，險者難知，易者易知，此特系夫人之險易者然也。

translations.literal: In human truth and deception there is the easy-to-know and the hard-to-know; the hard-to-know is difficult to understand, the easy-to-know is easy to understand—this merely depends on whether the person is hard or easy to know.
translations.idiomatic: People may be sincere or deceitful, easy to read or hard; that alone depends on the person—but there is more.

sentences.zh: 然又有眾寡之分焉。

translations.literal: Yet there is also the distinction of few versus many.
translations.idiomatic: There is also the question of numbers.

sentences.zh: 寡則易知，眾則難知，故在上者難於知下，而在下者易於知上，其勢然也。

translations.literal: When few, easy to know; when many, hard to know—thus those above find it hard to know those below, while those below find it easy to know those above; such is the force of circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: The few are easier to know than the many; hence those above struggle to know those below, while those below easily know those above. Such is the balance of power.

sentences.zh: 處難知之地，禦難知之人，欲其不見欺也難矣。

translations.literal: Standing in a hard-to-know position, facing hard-to-know men—wishing not to be deceived is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: To stand where knowledge is hard and face men who are hard to read—how can one hope never to be deceived?

sentences.zh: 昔包拯剛嚴峭直，號為明察，然一小吏而能欺之。

translations.literal: In former times Bao Zheng was stern, rigorous, and upright, famed as penetrating in judgment—yet a petty clerk was able to deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Zheng was famous for stern probity and keen insight—yet a lowly clerk still fooled him once.

sentences.zh: 然拯一京尹耳，其見欺於人，不過誤一事、害一人而已。

translations.literal: Yet Bao Zheng was only a capital prefect; his being deceived meant no more than one affair mistaken, one person harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Zheng was only the capital prefect; when deceived, at worst one case went wrong and one person suffered.

sentences.zh: 人君處億兆之上，操予奪進退賞罰生殺之權，不幸見欺，則以非為是，以是為非，其害有不可勝既也。

translations.literal: The ruler stands above hundreds of millions, wielding the power to grant and withhold, advance and dismiss, reward and punish, spare and kill; if unhappily deceived, wrong becomes right and right wrong—the harm is beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler stands above millions, holding life, death, reward, and ruin in his hand. If he is deceived, falsehood passes for truth and truth for falsehood—and the harm is beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 人君惟無喜怒也，有喜怒，則贊其喜以市恩，鼓其怒以張勢。

translations.literal: The ruler must be without joy and anger; with joy and anger, men will praise his joy to purchase favor and stir his anger to expand their power.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler must show neither joy nor anger; where joy and anger appear, men will inflame his pleasure to win favor and his wrath to build power.

sentences.zh: 人君惟無愛憎也，有愛憎，則假其愛以濟私，藉其憎以復怨。

translations.literal: The ruler must be without love and hatred; with love and hatred, men will borrow his love to serve private ends and borrow his hatred to settle old scores.
translations.idiomatic: He must harbor neither favor nor dislike; favor invites private uses of his love, dislike invites revenge through his hatred.

sentences.zh: 甚至本無喜也，誑之使喜，本無怒也，激之使怒，本不足愛也，而誑譽之使愛，本無可憎也，而強短之使憎。

translations.literal: To the point that when there was no joy, they deceived him into joy; when there was no anger, they provoked anger; when there was no cause for love, they flattered him into love; when there was nothing to hate, they forced faults upon others to make him hate.
translations.idiomatic: Men will feign grounds for joy where there was none, provoke anger where none existed, praise the unworthy into favor, and invent faults to breed hatred.

sentences.zh: 若是，則進者未必為君子，退者未必為小人，予者未必為有功，奪者未必為有罪，以至賞之、罰之、生之、殺之，鮮有得其正者。

translations.literal: If so, those advanced are not necessarily gentlemen; those dismissed not necessarily petty men; those granted not necessarily meritorious; those stripped not necessarily guilty—so that in reward, punishment, sparing, and killing, few hit what is right.
translations.idiomatic: Then promotion need not mean virtue, dismissal need not mean vice, reward need not mark merit, and punishment need not mark guilt. Life and death, reward and ruin—rarely fall where they should.

sentences.zh: 人君不悟其受欺也，而反任之以防天下之欺，欺而至此，尚可防邪？

translations.literal: The ruler does not realize he is being deceived, yet instead entrusts such men to guard against deception under Heaven—deception having reached this point, can it still be guarded against?
translations.idiomatic: Blind to his own deception, he yet relies on deceivers to guard against fraud. When fraud has gone this far, what is left to guard?

sentences.zh: 大抵人君以知人為貴，以用人為急。

translations.literal: Broadly, for a ruler, knowing men is prized; employing men is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: In general, a ruler's chief treasure is knowing men and his most urgent task is using them well.

sentences.zh: 用得其人，則無事於防矣。

translations.literal: Employ the right men, and there is no need for guarding.
translations.idiomatic: Employ the right men, and guarding becomes unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 既不出此，則所近者爭進之人耳，好利之人耳，無恥之人耳。

translations.literal: Since one does not proceed from this, those who draw near are merely men scrambling to advance, men who love profit, men without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Fail at that, and those who surround the throne are climbers, profiteers, and men without shame.

sentences.zh: 彼挾其詐術，千蹊萬徑，以蠱君心，欲防其欺，雖堯、舜不能也。

translations.literal: They wield their crafty arts by a thousand paths and ten thousand routes to bewitch the ruler's heart; wishing to guard against their deception—even Yao and Shun could not.
translations.idiomatic: Armed with every trick and bypath, they beguile the ruler's mind. To block such deception—even Yao and Shun would fail.

sentences.zh: 夫賢者以公為心，以愛為心，不為利回，不為勢屈，置之周行，則庶事得其正，天下被其澤，其於人國，重固如此也。

translations.literal: The worthy take public interest as their heart, loving care as their heart; they are not turned by profit, not bent by power; set among the chief ministers, then the myriad affairs gain their right course and all under Heaven receive their benefit—for the realm of men, the weight is indeed thus.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy serve the public good, not private gain; they bow neither to profit nor to power. Placed among the chief ministers, they set every affair straight and shower the realm with benefit. Their weight to the state is exactly this.

sentences.zh: 夫賢者遭時不偶，務自韜晦，世固未易知也。

translations.literal: The worthy, meeting times that do not favor them, strive to conceal themselves; the world naturally does not easily know them.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy, when fortune fails them, hide their light; the world does not easily recognize them.

sentences.zh: 雖或知之，而無所援引，則人君無由知也。

translations.literal: Though some may know them, if there is no one to recommend them, the ruler has no means to know them.
translations.idiomatic: Even when someone knows them, without a patron to bring them forward the ruler never will.

sentences.zh: 人君知之，然召之命之，泛如廝養，賢者有不屑也。

translations.literal: The ruler may know them, yet when summoning and appointing them treats them casually like stable hands—the worthy will disdain such treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the ruler knows them, a summons handled like a call to the stables will make the worthy refuse to come.

sentences.zh: 雖或接之以貌，待之以禮，然而言不見用，賢者不處也。

translations.literal: Though one may receive them with proper appearance and treat them with ritual, if their words are not employed, the worthy will not remain.
translations.idiomatic: Courtesy without heeding their counsel will not keep the worthy in service.

sentences.zh: 或用其言也，而復使小人參之，責小利，期近效，有用賢之名，無用賢之實，賢者亦豈肯屍位素餐以取譏於天下哉！

translations.literal: Or one may use their words yet again set petty men alongside them, demanding small profit and expecting near-term results—having the name of employing the worthy without the reality; would the worthy consent to hold office in name only and eat salary without work, inviting ridicule under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Or their counsel is taken but petty men share the task, small gains are demanded, quick results expected—the name of employing worthies without the reality. Would the worthy hold a hollow post and invite the world's scorn?

sentences.zh: 此特難進者也，而又有​​難合者焉。

translations.literal: These are merely the hard-to-advance; yet there are also the hard-to-harmonize-with.
translations.idiomatic: These are men hard to bring forward—and there are also men hard to work with.

sentences.zh: 人君處崇高之地，大抵樂聞人過，而不樂於聞己之過，務快己之心，而不務快民之心。

translations.literal: The ruler stands in an exalted place; broadly he delights in hearing others' faults, but not in hearing his own; he strives to please his own heart, not to please the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler in high place loves to hear others' faults but not his own, seeks his own pleasure rather than the people's contentment.

sentences.zh: 賢者必欲匡而正之，扶而安之，如堯、舜之正、堯、舜之安而後已，故其勢恆難合​​。

translations.literal: The worthy must wish to correct and set right, support and settle secure—as Yao and Shun set right, as Yao and Shun settled secure—only then stopping; hence the tendency is always hard to harmonize with.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy must set things right and secure the realm, as Yao and Shun did, and will not stop short of that—so harmony with the throne is always hard.

sentences.zh: 況夫奸邪佞幸，醜正而惡直，肆為詆毀，多方以陷之，將見罪戾之不免，又可望其庶事得其正，而天下被其澤邪！

translations.literal: How much more when treacherous, wicked, and fawning favorites hate the upright and loathe the straight, wantonly slandering and scheming by many means to entrap them—guilt and punishment will soon be unavoidable; how then can one expect that the myriad affairs gain their right course and all under Heaven receive benefit?
translations.idiomatic: When sycophants hate the upright and invent charges to destroy them, guilt follows—and how then can affairs be set right or the realm blessed?

sentences.zh: 自古及今，端人雅士所以重於進而輕於退者，蓋以此耳。

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present, upright men and refined scholars have valued withdrawal over advancement—this is broadly the reason.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present, upright scholars have prized withdrawal over advancement—for this very reason.

sentences.zh: 大禹聖人，聞善即拜，益猶戒之以「任賢勿貳，去邪勿疑」，後世人主宜如何也？

translations.literal: Great Yu was a sage; hearing goodness he at once bowed in respect—yet Yi still admonished him, "Employ the worthy without wavering; remove the wicked without doubt." How ought later rulers conduct themselves?
translations.idiomatic: Great Yu, a sage, bowed at the mere report of good counsel—yet Yi still warned him, "Employ the worthy without wavering; remove the wicked without doubt." What should later rulers do?

sentences.zh: 此任賢之難也。

translations.literal: This is the difficulty of employing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the difficulty of employing the worthy.

sentences.zh: 奸邪之人，其為心也險，其用術也巧。

translations.literal: Treacherous and wicked men—their hearts are perilous, their arts crafty.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous men have perilous hearts and crafty methods.

sentences.zh: 惟險也，故千態萬狀而人莫能知；

translations.literal: Because they are perilous, they assume a thousand forms and ten thousand shapes, and no one can know them.
translations.idiomatic: Their perilous nature takes a thousand forms, beyond anyone's reading;

sentences.zh: 惟巧也，故千蹊萬徑而人莫能禦。

translations.literal: Because they are crafty, they follow a thousand paths and ten thousand routes, and no one can guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: their craft opens a thousand paths, beyond anyone's defense.

sentences.zh: 其諂似恭，其訐似直，其欺似可信，其佞似可近。

translations.literal: Their flattery seems respectful, their accusations seem straight, their deception seems trustworthy, their sycophancy seems approachable.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery that looks like respect, accusation that looks like honesty, deceit that looks trustworthy, sycophancy that looks approachable.

sentences.zh: 務以窺人君之喜怒而迎合之，竊其勢以立己之威，濟其欲以結主之愛。

translations.literal: They strive to spy out the ruler's joy and anger and meet them; they steal his power to establish their own authority, and serve his desires to bind the lord's affection.
translations.idiomatic: They watch the ruler's moods and pander to them, borrow his power to build their own, and feed his desires to win his favor.

sentences.zh: 愛隆於上，威擅於下，大臣不敢議，近親不敢言，毒被天下而上莫之知，至是而求去之，亦已難矣。

translations.literal: Favor rises above, authority is monopolized below; great ministers dare not debate, close kin dare not speak; poison spreads under Heaven while the ruler knows nothing—by then to seek their removal is already difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Favor at court, power in their hands, ministers silent and kin afraid—the poison spreads while the ruler knows nothing. By then removal is nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 雖然，此特人主之不悟者也，猶有說焉。

translations.literal: Even so, this is merely the case of a ruler who does not awaken—there is still something to be said.
translations.idiomatic: Even this may be excused as the blindness of an unwary ruler.

sentences.zh: 如宇文士及之佞，太宗灼見其情而不能斥；

translations.literal: Such as Yuwen Shiji's sycophancy—Taizong saw his disposition clearly yet could not dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shiji's flattery was plain to Emperor Taizong, yet he could not dismiss him;

sentences.zh: 李林甫妒賢嫉能，明皇洞見其奸而不能退。

translations.literal: Li Linfu envied the worthy and hated ability; Emperor Ming saw through his treachery yet could not remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu envied talent; Emperor Xuanzong saw his treachery yet could not remove him.

sentences.zh: 邪之惑人，有如此者，可不畏哉！

translations.literal: Evil's power to bewitch men can be thus—should one not fear it!
translations.idiomatic: Evil can beguile men to this degree—should it not inspire dread?

sentences.zh: 夫上以誠愛下，則下以忠報上，感應之理然也。

translations.literal: When those above sincerely love those below, those below repay with loyalty—such is the principle of mutual response.
translations.idiomatic: When rulers love their people sincerely, the people repay with loyalty—that is the natural order of response.

sentences.zh: 然考之往昔，有不可以常情論者。

translations.literal: Yet examining the past, there are cases that cannot be judged by ordinary sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet history shows cases that ordinary reasoning cannot explain.

sentences.zh: 禹抑洪水以救民，啟又能敬承繼禹之道，其澤深矣，然一傳而太康失道，則萬姓仇怨而去者，何邪？

translations.literal: Yu restrained the floodwaters to save the people; Qi was able reverently to inherit and continue Yu's Way—their beneficence was deep; yet one transmission later Taikang lost the Way, and the myriad people departed in hatred and resentment—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yu tamed the floods to save the people; Qi reverently carried on his Way. Their grace ran deep—yet one generation later Taikang lost the Way and the people turned away in hatred. Why?

sentences.zh: 漢高帝起布衣，天下影從，滎陽之難，紀信至捐生以赴急，則人心之歸可見矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han rose from common cloth; all under Heaven followed like shadows; at the crisis of Xingyang, Ji Xin even gave his life to meet the emergency—the people's hearts turning to him can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu rose from commoner ranks; the realm followed him. At the crisis of Xingyang, Ji Xin gave his life for the cause—the depth of popular loyalty was plain.

sentences.zh: 及天下己定，而沙中有謀反者，又何邪？

translations.literal: When all under Heaven was settled, yet there were plotters of rebellion in the sands—why again?
translations.idiomatic: Yet once the realm was settled, rebels still rose from the deserts. Why?

sentences.zh: 竊嘗思之，民之戴君，本於天命，初無不順之心，特由使之失望，使之不平，然後怨怒生焉。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately pondered: the people's support of their ruler rests on Heaven's mandate; at first there is no heart of disobedience—it is only that being made to lose hope and being made to feel injustice, then resentment and anger arise.
translations.idiomatic: I have reflected on this: the people support their ruler by Heaven's mandate and begin without disloyalty. Resentment arises only when hope is betrayed and justice denied.

sentences.zh: 禹、啟愛民如赤子，而太康逸豫以滅德，是以失望；

translations.literal: Yu and Qi loved the people as infants; yet Taikang indulged in ease and pleasure and destroyed virtue—thus hope was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Qi loved the people as their own children; Taikang indulged himself and lost virtue—hence the people's disappointment.

sentences.zh: 漢高以寬仁得天下，及其已定，乃以愛憎行誅賞，是以不平。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu won all under Heaven through leniency and benevolence; when it was settled, he then meted out punishment and reward according to love and hatred—thus injustice arose.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu won the realm through leniency and grace; once secure, he punished and rewarded by personal favor and spite—hence the people's sense of injustice.

sentences.zh: 古今人君，凡有恩澤於民，而民怨且怒者，皆類此也。

translations.literal: Rulers ancient and modern who had shown grace to the people yet were met with popular resentment and anger—all resemble this.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers ancient and modern who had once blessed the people yet earned their anger have all followed this pattern.

sentences.zh: 夫人君有位之初，既出美言而告天下矣，既而實不能副，故怨生焉。

translations.literal: When a ruler first takes his place, he has already issued fine words to announce them to all under Heaven; afterward the reality cannot match—thus resentment arises.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of a reign, fine promises are proclaimed to the realm; when reality falls short, resentment follows.

sentences.zh: 等人臣耳，無大相遠，人君特以己之私而厚一人，則其薄者已疾之矣，況於薄有功而厚有罪，人得不怒於心邪？

translations.literal: Ministers are all alike, not greatly different; if the ruler merely by private feeling enriches one man, those he treats thinly already resent it—how much more when the meritorious are treated thinly and the guilty treated richly; can people not rage in their hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Ministers differ little among themselves; favor one by private whim and the rest already resent it. Reward the guilty and slight the meritorious—who would not rage inwardly?

sentences.zh: 必如古者《大學》之道，以修身為本，一言一動，舉可以為天下之法，一賞一罰，舉可以合天下之公，則億兆之心，將不求而自得，又豈有失望不平之累哉！

translations.literal: One must be like the ancients in the Way of the Great Learning, taking self-cultivation as root—every word and act can serve as law for all under Heaven; every reward and punishment can accord with public justice under Heaven—then the hearts of hundreds of millions will be gained without seeking, and how could there remain the burden of lost hope and injustice!
translations.idiomatic: Follow the Great Learning: root every word and deed in self-cultivation, let every act be a model for the realm and every reward and punishment serve the public good—then the hearts of millions will come unbidden, and disappointment and injustice will vanish.

sentences.zh: 三代而下，稱盛治者，無如漢之文、景，然考之當時，天象數變，山崩地震，未易遽數，是將小則有水旱之災，大則有亂亡之應，非徒然而已也。

translations.literal: From the Three Dynasties downward, those called flourishing in governance were none like Emperors Wen and Jing of Han—yet examining their time, celestial signs changed repeatedly, mountains collapsed and the earth quaked, not easily counted at once; this meant that on the small scale there were flood and drought disasters, on the large scale responses of disorder and ruin—not merely for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Three Dynasties, no reign has been praised as well governed as those of Emperors Wen and Jing—yet even then the heavens shifted, mountains fell, and the earth shook without end, foretelling drought and flood at least and chaos and ruin at worst. Such signs are never idle.

sentences.zh: 而文、景克承天心，一以養民為務，今年勸農桑，明年減田租，懇愛如此，宜其民心得而和氣應也。

translations.literal: Yet Wen and Jing were able to inherit Heaven's heart, making nurturing the people their sole task—this year encouraging farming and sericulture, next year reducing land tax; such earnest love—fitting that the people's hearts were won and harmonious qi responded.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wen and Jing answered Heaven's will by making the people's welfare their sole concern—encouraging farming one year, cutting land tax the next. With such earnest care, hearts were won and harmony restored.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見前年秋孛出西方，彗出東方，去年冬彗見東方，復見西方。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately observed: the autumn before last, a broom star appeared in the west and a comet in the east; last winter a comet appeared in the east and again in the west.
translations.idiomatic: I note that two autumns ago a broom star rose in the west and a comet in the east; last winter comets appeared in the east and again in the west.

sentences.zh: 議者謂當除舊佈新，以應天變。

translations.literal: Counselors say one should remove the old and spread the new, to respond to Heaven's changes.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors say the court should sweep out the old and usher in the new to answer Heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 臣以為曷若直法文、景之恭儉愛民，為理明義正而可信也。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that how much better to follow directly the reverent thrift and love of the people shown by Wen and Jing—governing with clarity of principle and rectitude of justice, and thus being trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: I believe it would be better to follow Wen and Jing in reverent thrift and love of the people—governing with clear principle and upright justice that men can trust.

sentences.zh: 天之樹君，本為下民。

translations.literal: Heaven establishes rulers fundamentally for the people below.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sets up rulers for the sake of the people.

sentences.zh: 故孟子謂「民為重，君為輕」，《書》亦曰「天視自我民視，天聽自我民聽」。

translations.literal: Thus Mencius said, "The people are heavy, the ruler is light"; the Documents also says, "Heaven sees as my people see, Heaven hears as my people hear."
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, "The people are paramount, the ruler is secondary." The Documents says, "Heaven sees through the people's eyes and hears through the people's ears."

sentences.zh: 以是論之，則天之道恆在於下，恆在於不足也。

translations.literal: Judging by this, Heaven's Way constantly rests with those below, constantly rests with what is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: By this reckoning, Heaven's Way always sides with those below and with what is lacking.

sentences.zh: 君人者，不求之下而求之高，不求之不足而求之有餘，斯其所以召天變也。

translations.literal: One who rules men does not seek among those below but among those above, does not seek among the insufficient but among the surplus—this is what summons Heaven's changes.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who looks upward rather than downward, to abundance rather than need—that is what summons Heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 其變已生，其像已著，乖戾之幾已萌，猶且因仍故習，抑其下而損其不足，謂之順天，不亦難乎？

translations.literal: The change has already arisen, the portent already shown, the seeds of perversity already sprouted—yet one still follows old habits, pressing down those below and cutting what is insufficient, calling it obeying Heaven—is this not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: When signs have already appeared and perversity has taken root, yet the court clings to old ways, presses the lowly and strips the needy, and calls it obeying Heaven—is that not folly?

sentences.zh: 此六者，皆難之目也。

translations.literal: These six are all items of difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: These six are the headings of difficulty.

sentences.zh: 舉其要，則修德、用賢、愛民三者而已。

translations.literal: Taken in essence, there are only three: cultivating virtue, employing the worthy, and loving the people.
translations.idiomatic: In essence, there are only three: cultivate virtue, employ the worthy, and love the people.

sentences.zh: 此謂治本。

translations.literal: This is called treating the root.
translations.idiomatic: This is treating the root cause.

sentences.zh: 本立，則紀綱可布，法度可行，治功可必。

translations.literal: Once the root is established, the framework can be laid out, laws and standards can be carried out, and governing achievement can be assured.
translations.idiomatic: Once the root is set, order can be established, law enforced, and good governance assured.

sentences.zh: 否則愛惡相攻，善惡交病，生民不免於水火，以是為治，萬不能也。

translations.literal: Otherwise love and hatred attack each other, good and evil mutually afflict; the living people cannot escape flood and fire—to take this as governance is utterly impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise favor and spite war with each other, good and evil both suffer, and the people cannot escape ruin. Governance on such terms is impossible.

sentences.zh: 其四曰：語古之聖君，必曰堯、舜；

translations.literal: The fourth point says: speaking of sage rulers of antiquity, one must name Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: when one speaks of sage rulers of old, one names Yao and Shun;

sentences.zh: 語古之賢相，必曰稷、契。

translations.literal: Speaking of worthy ministers of antiquity, one must name Ji and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: when one speaks of worthy ministers, one names Ji and Qi.

sentences.zh: 蓋堯、舜能知天道而順承之，稷、契又知堯、舜之心而輔讚之，此所以為法於天下，可傳於後世也。

translations.literal: For Yao and Shun were able to know Heaven's Way and follow and inherit it; Ji and Qi in turn knew Yao and Shun's hearts and assisted and praised them—this is why they became models for all under Heaven and can be transmitted to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun knew Heaven's Way and followed it; Ji and Qi knew their rulers' hearts and supported them. That is why they became models for the realm and examples for posterity.

sentences.zh: 夫天道好生而不私，堯與舜亦好生而不私。

translations.literal: Heaven's Way loves life and is without partiality; Yao and Shun also loved life and were without partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way cherishes life without partiality; Yao and Shun cherished life without partiality.

sentences.zh: 若「克明俊德」，至於「黎民於變」，「敬授人時」，至於「庶績咸熙」，此順承天道之實也。

translations.literal: Such as "making illustrious his lofty virtue," reaching to "the common people being transformed"; "respectfully conferring the seasons upon men," reaching to "all achievements flourishing together"—this is the reality of following and inheriting Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: From "making illustrious his lofty virtue" to "the people transformed," from "respectfully conferring the seasons" to "all tasks flourishing"—that is what it means to follow Heaven's Way.

sentences.zh: 稷播百穀以厚民生，契敷五教以善民心，此輔贊堯、舜之實也。

translations.literal: Ji spread the hundred grains to enrich the people's livelihood; Qi spread the five teachings to improve the people's hearts—this is the reality of assisting and praising Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sowed the hundred grains to nourish the people; Qi spread the five teachings to improve their hearts—that is what it means to support Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗复熟推衍，思之又思，參之往古聖賢之言無不同，驗之歷代治亂之跡無不合。

translations.literal: Your servant has repeatedly pondered and deduced, thinking again and again; comparing with the words of sages and worthies of old, there is no disagreement; verifying against the traces of order and disorder through the dynasties, there is no mismatch.
translations.idiomatic: I have pondered this again and again: it matches the words of every sage of old and the record of every age's rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 蓋此道之行，民可使富，兵可使強，人才可使盛，國勢可使重，夙夜念之至熟也。

translations.literal: Broadly, when this Way is practiced, the people can be made rich, the army strong, talent abundant, and national strength weighty—your servant has pondered it day and night to full ripeness.
translations.idiomatic: When this Way is followed, the people grow rich, armies grow strong, talent flourishes, and the state's weight increases—I have thought on this day and night.

sentences.zh: 今國家徒知斂財之巧，而不知生財之由；

translations.literal: Now the state merely knows the craft of gathering wealth, but does not know the source of generating wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Today the state knows only tricks for extracting revenue, not the roots of creating wealth;

sentences.zh: 徒知防人之欺，而不欲養人之善；

translations.literal: Merely knows guarding against men's deception, but does not wish to nurture men's goodness.
translations.idiomatic: knows only how to guard against fraud, not how to cultivate virtue;

sentences.zh: 徒患法令之難行，而不患法令無可行之地。

translations.literal: Merely worries that laws and commands are hard to enforce, but does not worry that laws and commands have no place where they can be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: worries only that laws are hard to enforce, not that there is no ground on which law can take hold.

sentences.zh: 誠能優重農民，勿擾勿害，驅遊惰之人而歸之南畝，課之種藝，懇喻而督行之，十年之後，倉府之積，當非今日之比矣。

translations.literal: If one can truly honor and weight the farmers, neither harassing nor harming them, driving idle and lazy men back to the southern fields, assigning them planting and cultivation, earnestly instructing and supervising them—in ten years' time, the stores of granaries and treasuries should be incomparable with today.
translations.idiomatic: Truly honor farmers, leave them undisturbed, drive the idle back to the fields, assign planting and cultivation, and earnestly supervise—in ten years the granaries would bear no comparison to today.

sentences.zh: 自都邑而至州縣，皆設學校，使皇子以下至於庶人之子弟，皆入於學，以明父子君臣之大倫，自灑掃應對以至平天下之要道，十年已後，上知所以御下，下知所以事上，上下和睦，又非今日之比矣。

translations.literal: From the capital down to prefectures and counties, schools should all be established, so that from the princes downward to the sons of commoners, all enter study—to clarify the great relations of father and son, ruler and minister, from sweeping and responding to the essential Way of bringing peace to all under Heaven; ten years later, those above will know how to govern those below, those below will know how to serve those above, above and below harmonious—again incomparable with today.
translations.idiomatic: Establish schools from the capital to every county, so that princes and commoners' sons alike may study the great relations of family and state—from daily conduct to the art of governing the realm. In ten years rulers will know how to lead and subjects how to serve, and harmony above and below will surpass anything seen today.

sentences.zh: 二者之行，萬目斯舉，否則他皆不可期也。

translations.literal: If these two are practiced, ten thousand eyes will lift together; otherwise nothing else can be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Carry out these two measures and all else may follow; without them, nothing else can be hoped for.

sentences.zh: 是道也，堯、舜之道也。

translations.literal: This Way is the Way of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: This is the Way of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：「我非堯、舜之道，不敢以陳於王前。」

translations.literal: Mencius said, "What is not the Way of Yao and Shun, I dare not set forth before the king."
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, "I dare not set before the king any counsel that is not the Way of Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 臣愚區區，竊亦願學也。

translations.literal: Your servant, small and humble, also privately wishes to learn.
translations.idiomatic: I am small and humble, but I too wish to learn this Way.

sentences.zh: 其五曰：天下所以定者，民志定，則士安於士，農安於農，工商安於為工商，則在上之人有可安之理矣。

translations.literal: The fifth point says: what settles all under Heaven is the settling of the people's will; when the people's will is settled, then scholars rest in being scholars, farmers in being farmers, artisans and merchants in being artisans and merchants—then those above have grounds on which they may rest secure.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: the realm is settled when the people's will is settled. Let scholars rest in scholarship, farmers in farming, artisans and merchants in their trades—then those above may also rest secure.

sentences.zh: 夫民不安於白屋，必求祿仕；

translations.literal: When the people are not secure in plain thatched houses, they must seek salary and office.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners cannot rest content in humble homes, they seek office and salary;

sentences.zh: 仕不安於卑位，必求尊榮。

translations.literal: When office-holders are not secure in low rank, they must seek honor and glory.
translations.idiomatic: when officials cannot rest in low rank, they seek honor and glory.

sentences.zh: 四方萬里，輻輳並進，各懷無厭無恥之心，在上之人可不為寒心哉！

translations.literal: From the four quarters, ten thousand li, they converge and advance together, each harboring hearts without satiety and without shame—should not those above be chilled at heart!
translations.idiomatic: From every corner of the realm they press forward together, each with insatiable and shameless ambition—should those above not shudder?

sentences.zh: 臣聞取天下者尚勇敢，守天下者尚退讓。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that he who takes the realm values courage, while he who keeps the realm values yielding.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that conquering the realm calls for boldness, but holding it calls for restraint.

sentences.zh: 取也守也，各有其宜，君人者不可不審也。

translations.literal: Taking and keeping each have their proper measure; one who rules men cannot but weigh this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Conquest and governance each have their proper season; a ruler must discern which applies when.

sentences.zh: 夫審而後發，發無不中，否則觸事而遽喜怒，喜怒之色見於貌，言出於口，人皆知之。

translations.literal: When one deliberates and then acts, action never misses its mark; otherwise, encountering affairs one hastily rejoices or grows angry—the colors of joy and anger show in the countenance, words issue from the mouth, and all know it.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberate first, and every act hits its mark; fail to do so, and joy or anger flares at the first provocation—everyone reads it on your face and hears it in your words.

sentences.zh: 徐考其故，知其無可喜者則必悔其喜之失，無可怒者則必悔其怒之失，甚至先喜而後怒，先怒而後喜，號令數變，喜怒不節之故也。

translations.literal: Slow to examine the cause, knowing there is nothing to rejoice in one must regret the error of rejoicing; knowing there is nothing to rage at one must regret the error of rage—even to rejoicing first and then raging, raging first and then rejoicing, orders changing repeatedly, all from failure to restrain joy and anger.
translations.idiomatic: Only afterward do you see there was nothing to celebrate and regret your elation, or nothing to condemn and regret your fury—joy turns to wrath, wrath to joy, commands shift with your mood. Such is the cost of an undisciplined heart.

sentences.zh: 是以先王潛心恭默，不易喜怒，其未發也，雖至近莫能知其發也，雖至親莫能移，是以號令簡而無悔，則無不中節矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings concealed the heart in reverent silence, not lightly changing joy and anger; before they issued forth, though the closest could not know when they would issue forth, though the nearest kin could not sway them—thus commands were simple and without regret, and none failed to hit the proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings kept their hearts inward and still, seldom showing pleasure or displeasure. Before they acted, even those closest could not guess what they would do, nor could the dearest move them from their resolve. Their commands were few and never regretted, and always struck the proper measure.

sentences.zh: 夫數變，不可也；

translations.literal: To change repeatedly—this cannot be done;
translations.idiomatic: Constant change—this cannot be tolerated;

sentences.zh: 數失信，尤不可也。

translations.literal: to lose trust repeatedly—this especially cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: and repeated breaches of trust—least of all.

sentences.zh: 周幽無道，故不恤此，今無此，何苦使人之不信也。

translations.literal: King You of Zhou was without the Way, and therefore did not heed this—but today there is no such case; why bring upon men disbelief?
translations.idiomatic: King You of Zhou had lost the Way and cared nothing for such things—but Your Majesty is not he. Why give your subjects cause to doubt you?

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, and the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised it and took its counsel to heart.

sentences.zh: 衡自見帝，多奏陳，及退，皆削其草，故其言多秘，世罕得聞，所傳者特此耳。

translations.literal: Whenever Heng had an audience with the Emperor, he often submitted memorials; when he withdrew, he always destroyed the drafts—therefore his words were mostly secret, the world rarely heard them, and what has come down is only this.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Heng had audience with the Emperor he submitted many memorials, but on leaving he always destroyed the drafts. Most of his counsel remained secret; the world rarely heard it, and only this much has been preserved.

sentences.zh: 衡多病，帝聽五日一至省，時賜尚方名藥美酒以調養之。

translations.literal: Heng was often ill; the Emperor allowed him to visit the palace once every five days and from time to time bestowed famed drugs and fine wine from the imperial pharmacy for his nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Heng suffered frequent illness. The Emperor permitted him to attend court every five days and sent him choice medicines and wine from the imperial dispensary.

sentences.zh: 四年，乃聽其歸懷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was finally allowed to return to Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was at last permitted to return home to Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，復召還，奏對亦秘。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was summoned back; his responses at audience were also kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled to court; his responses there, too, went unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 六年，命與太常卿徐世隆定朝儀，儀成，帝臨觀，甚悅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was ordered together with Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Xu Shilong to fix the court ceremonies; when the ceremonies were completed, the Emperor came in person to observe and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was charged, with Director Xu Shilong of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, to establish court ritual. When the rites were complete the Emperor observed them in person and was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 又詔與太保劉秉忠、左丞張文謙定官制，衡歷考古今分並統屬之序，去其權攝增置冗長側置者，凡省部、院台、郡縣與夫后妃、儲籓、百司所聯屬統制，定為圖。

translations.literal: He was also ordered together with Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong and Left Director Zhang Wenqian to fix the official system; Heng examined through past and present the order of division, merger, and subordination, removed provisional powers, redundant additions, and side placements, and for the ministries, the Academies, the Censorate, prefectures and counties, and the linkage and control of empresses, imperial sons, and the hundred offices, fixed them in a chart.
translations.idiomatic: He was also instructed, with Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong and Left Director Zhang Wenqian, to design the bureaucracy. Heng mapped how offices had been divided, merged, and subordinated through history, stripped away provisional powers and redundant posts, and set out in charts the lines of authority among ministries, academies, the Censorate, prefectures and counties, the imperial household, and every branch of government.

sentences.zh: 七年，奏上之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he submitted it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh year it was submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 翌日，使集公卿雜議中書、院台行移之體，衡曰：「中書佐天子總國政，院台宜具呈。」

translations.literal: The next day, he was made to assemble the high officials to discuss miscellaneous matters regarding the forms of official communication between the Secretariat, the Academies, and the Censorate. Heng said, "The Secretariat assists the Son of Heaven in governing the state; the Academies and Censorate ought to submit memorials for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was directed to gather the senior officials to debate how the Secretariat, the Academies, and the Censorate should exchange documents. Heng said, "The Secretariat assists the Son of Heaven in governing the realm; the Academies and Censorate should submit memorials for his review.

sentences.zh: 時商挺在樞密，高鳴在台，皆不樂，欲定為諮禀，因大言以動衡曰：「台院皆宗親大臣，若一忤，禍不可測。」

translations.literal: At the time Shang Ting was in the Privy Council and Gao Ming was in the Censorate, both displeased, wishing to fix it as consultation and reporting; they therefore spoke grandly to move Heng, saying, "The Censorate and Academies are all imperial kinsmen and great ministers—if you offend one, disaster cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ting sat on the Privy Council and Gao Ming in the Censorate; both were displeased and wanted all communications routed through consultation and submission. They tried to intimidate Heng: "The Censorate and Academies are staffed by imperial kin and great ministers. Offend one of them and the consequences are incalculable.

sentences.zh: 衡曰：「吾論國製耳，何與於人？」

translations.literal: Heng said, "I speak of the national system—what has this to do with individuals?
translations.idiomatic: Heng replied, "I speak of the national order. What has that to do with anyone's personal standing?

sentences.zh: 遂以其言質帝前，帝曰：「衡言是也，吾意亦若是。」

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted his words to be tested before the Emperor; the Emperor said, "What Heng says is correct; my mind is likewise."
translations.idiomatic: He put the question directly to the Emperor, who said, "Heng is right. That is my view as well."

sentences.zh: 未幾，阿合馬為中書平章政事，領尚書省六部事，因擅權，勢傾朝野，一時大臣多阿之，衡每與之議，必正言不少讓。

translations.literal: Before long, Ahmad became Pingzhang of the Secretariat and took charge of the Six Ministries of the Department of State Affairs; thereby usurping power, his influence tipped the court and field, and for a time most great ministers fawned on him—Heng whenever he discussed with him always spoke uprightly and yielded not at all.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ahmad became co-director of the Secretariat and assumed control of the Six Ministries. His power overshadowed the court; most senior officials flattered him. Heng alone argued with him forthrightly and never yielded.

sentences.zh: 已而其子又有僉樞密院之命，衡獨執議曰：「國家事權，兵民財三者而已。

translations.literal: Soon after, his son also received an appointment as Vice-Director of the Privy Council; Heng alone held to his view, saying, "In state affairs there are only three powers: military, people, and finance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Emperor appointed Ahmad's son vice-director of the Privy Council. Heng alone objected: "State power rests on three pillars—arms, people, and revenue.

sentences.zh: 今其父典民與財，子又典兵，不可。」

translations.literal: Now the father controls the people and finance, and the son also controls the military—this cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: The father already controls the people and the treasury, and now the son would control the army. This cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿慮其反邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Do you fear that he will rebel?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Do you fear he will rebel?

sentences.zh: 衡對曰：「彼雖不反，此反道也。」

translations.literal: Heng replied, "Though he may not rebel, this is the way of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Heng replied, "He may never rebel, but this is the path to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬由是銜之，亟薦衡宜在中書，欲因以事中之。

translations.literal: Ahmad from this bore a grudge against him and urgently recommended that Heng ought to serve in the Secretariat, wishing thereby to entrap him through affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad nursed a grudge and promptly recommended Heng for a post in the Secretariat, hoping to trap him in some official misstep.

sentences.zh: 俄除左丞，衡屢入辭免，帝命左右掖衡出。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Left Director; Heng repeatedly entered to decline and request dismissal, and the Emperor ordered attendants to escort Heng out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Heng was appointed left director. He repeatedly petitioned to decline, until the Emperor ordered attendants to usher him from the hall.

sentences.zh: 衡出及閾，還奏曰：「陛下命臣出，豈出省邪？」

translations.literal: Heng went out as far as the threshold, then returned and reported, "Your Majesty ordered your subject to go out—does that mean to leave the Secretariat?
translations.idiomatic: Heng reached the threshold, then turned back and said, "Your Majesty ordered me out—do you mean out of the Secretariat?

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「出殿門耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "Only out the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed. "Only out the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 從幸上京，乃論列阿合馬專權罔上、蠹政害民若干事，不報。

translations.literal: Accompanying the Emperor on a visit to Shangjing, he thereupon enumerated several matters of Ahmad's monopolizing power, deceiving superiors, and corrupting government to harm the people—no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: On a journey to the upper capital with the Emperor, he submitted a detailed indictment of Ahmad's abuse of power, deception of the throne, and harm to the people. No answer came.

sentences.zh: 因謝病請解機務。

translations.literal: He thereupon pleaded illness and requested release from weighty duties.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness and asked to be relieved of his duties.

sentences.zh: 帝惻然，召其子師可入，諭旨，且命舉自代者。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved with compassion, summoned his son Shike to enter, conveyed the imperial intent, and also ordered him to recommend someone to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply moved. He summoned Heng's son Shike, conveyed his wishes, and asked Heng to name his successor.

sentences.zh: 衡奏曰：「用人，天子之大柄也。

translations.literal: Heng submitted, "The appointment of men is the great handle of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Heng replied, "The power to appoint officials belongs to the Son of Heaven alone.

sentences.zh: 臣下泛論其賢否則可，若授之以位，則當斷自宸衷，不可使臣下有市恩之漸也。」

translations.literal: For subjects broadly to discuss their worthiness or not is permissible, but if offices are conferred, the decision ought to be made from the imperial heart alone—subjects must not be allowed the first step toward currying favor by bestowing posts."
translations.idiomatic: A subject may speak generally of a man's merits, but to grant him office is for the Emperor alone. Ministers must not be given the first step toward trading in favors."

sentences.zh: 帝久欲開太學，會衡請罷益力，乃從其請。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long wished to open the Imperial Academy; as Heng's request to resign grew more forceful, he granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had long wished to establish the Imperial Academy; when Heng pressed harder to resign, he granted the request.

sentences.zh: 八年，以為集賢大學士，兼國子祭酒，親為擇蒙古弟子俾教之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was made Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies and concurrently Director of the Imperial Academy; the Emperor personally selected Mongol students for him to teach.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies and Director of the Imperial Academy. The Emperor personally chose Mongol youths for him to instruct.

sentences.zh: 衡聞命，喜曰：「此吾事也。

translations.literal: Heng upon receiving the appointment rejoiced and said, "This is my affair.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving the appointment Heng rejoiced. "This is the work I was born for.

sentences.zh: 國人子大樸未散，視聽專一，若置之善類中涵養數年，將必為國用。」

translations.literal: The sons of the realm are still unspoiled in their great simplicity, sight and hearing single-minded—if placed among good company and nurtured for several years, they will surely serve the state.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of the realm are still unformed and wholly attentive. Place them among worthy teachers for a few years and they will surely serve the state.

sentences.zh: 乃請徵其弟子王梓、劉季偉、韓思永、耶律有尚、呂端善、姚燧、高凝、白棟、蘇鬱、姚敦、孫安、劉安中十二人為伴讀。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested that twelve of his disciples be summoned—Wang Zi, Liu Jiwei, Han Siyong, Yelü Youshang, Lü Duanshan, Yao Sui, Gao Ning, Bai Dong, Su Yu, Yao Dun, Sun An, and Liu Anzhong—to serve as reading companions.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked that twelve of his own disciples be summoned as reading companions: Wang Zi, Liu Jiwei, Han Siyong, Yelü Youshang, Lü Duanshan, Yao Sui, Gao Ning, Bai Dong, Su Yu, Yao Dun, Sun An, and Liu Anzhong.

sentences.zh: 詔驛召之來京師，分處各齋，以為齋長。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them summoned by post relay to the capital; they were distributed among the various halls and made hall leaders.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned them by courier to the capital. They were assigned to separate halls and made hall leaders.

sentences.zh: 時所選弟子皆幼稚，衡待之如成人，愛之如子，出入進退，其嚴若君臣。

translations.literal: At the time the selected students were all young; Heng treated them as adults, loved them as sons, and in going out and coming in, advancing and withdrawing, was as strict as between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: The students chosen were all very young. Heng treated them as adults, loved them as sons, and in their comings and goings maintained a formality as strict as between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 其為教，因覺以明善，因明以開蔽，相其動息​​以為張弛。

translations.literal: In his teaching, through awakening he made goodness clear, through clarity he opened what was obscured, and gauging their movement and rest he set tension and release.
translations.idiomatic: In teaching he awakened them to goodness, used clarity to dispel confusion, and paced their work to their energy—tightening and loosening as they needed.

sentences.zh: 課誦少暇，即習禮，或習書算。

translations.literal: When there was a brief respite from recitation lessons, they at once practiced ritual, or practiced writing and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Between recitation sessions they practiced ritual, or writing and arithmetic.

sentences.zh: 少者則令習拜跪、揖讓、進退、應對，或射，或投壺，負者罰讀書若干遍。

translations.literal: The younger ones were made to practice bowing and kneeling, yielding with salutes, advancing and withdrawing, and responding to address; or they shot arrows, or played pitch-pot—the losers were punished by reading texts a set number of times.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest practiced bowing, saluting, entering and leaving, and formal address; they also shot arrows or played pitch-pot, with losers assigned extra readings.

sentences.zh: 久之，諸生人人自得，尊師敬業，下至童子，亦知三綱五常為生人之道。

translations.literal: After a long time, every student found his own footing, honored teachers and respected his work, and down to the youngest boys all knew the Three Bonds and Five Constants as the way of human life.
translations.idiomatic: In time every student found his footing, honored his teachers, and applied himself to his studies; even the youngest boys understood the Three Bonds and Five Constants as the foundation of a human life.

sentences.zh: 十年，權臣屢毀漢法，諸生廩食或不繼，衡請還懷。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, powerful ministers repeatedly undermined Han law; the students' grain stipends sometimes failed to continue, and Heng requested to return to Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year powerful ministers repeatedly attacked Chinese institutions; students' stipends sometimes went unpaid, and Heng asked to return to Huai.

sentences.zh: 帝以問翰林學士王磐，磐對曰：「衡教人有法，諸生行可從政，此國之大體，宜勿聽其去。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Hanlin Academician Wang Pan; Pan replied, "Heng has method in teaching men; the students' conduct qualifies them for government—this is a great principle of the state; he should not be allowed to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor consulted Hanlin Academician Wang Pan, who said, "Heng teaches with true method; his students are already fit for office. This is a pillar of the state—do not let him go.

sentences.zh: 帝命諸老臣議其去留，竇默為衡懇請之，乃聽衡還，以贊善王恂攝學事。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the senior ministers to discuss his departure or retention; Dou Mo earnestly pleaded on Heng's behalf, and he was finally allowed to return—Wang Xun, Instructor, was appointed to administer academy affairs in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked the senior ministers to decide. Dou Mo pleaded earnestly on Heng's behalf, and Heng was permitted to return home; Wang Xun was left in charge of the academy.

sentences.zh: 劉秉忠等奏，乞以衡弟子耶律有尚、蘇鬱、白棟為助教，以守衡規矩，從之。

translations.literal: Liu Bingzhong and others submitted, requesting that Heng's disciples Yelü Youshang, Su Yu, and Bai Dong be made assistant instructors to preserve Heng's rules—this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhong and others petitioned that Heng's disciples Yelü Youshang, Su Yu, and Bai Dong be made assistant instructors to preserve his methods. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 國家自得中原，用金《大明曆》，自大定是正後六七十年，氣朔加時漸差。

translations.literal: Since the state gained the Central Plains, it used the Jin Dynasty's Great Enlightenment Calendar; from the Dading era correction, sixty or seventy years later, the qi and new moon times gradually drifted.
translations.idiomatic: Since conquering the Central Plains the state had used the Jin calendar, the Great Enlightenment Calendar. Six or seven decades after its last correction in the Dading era, its reckonings of seasonal nodes and new moons had gradually fallen out of alignment.

sentences.zh: 帝以海宇混一，宜協時正日。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered that with the seas and lands unified, the times ought to be harmonized and the days corrected.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm unified under one rule, the Emperor held that heaven's times and the calendar should be brought into accord.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詔王恂定新歷。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, an edict ordered Wang Xun to fix a new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year an edict charged Wang Xun with drafting a new calendar.

sentences.zh: 恂以為歷家知歷數而不知歷理，宜得衡領之，乃以集賢大學士兼國子祭酒，教領太史院事，召至京。

translations.literal: Xun considered that calendar specialists know calendrical numbers but not calendrical principle, and that Heng ought to lead the work; he was therefore made Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies and concurrently Director of the Imperial Academy, instructed to head the affairs of the Directorate of Astronomy, and summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xun argued that astronomers knew the arithmetic of the calendar but not its underlying principles, and that Heng should lead the project. Heng was therefore made Grand Academician and Director of the Imperial Academy and charged to head the Directorate of Astronomy, then summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 衡以為冬至者歷之本，而求曆本者在驗氣。

translations.literal: Heng held that the winter solstice is the root of the calendar, and that seeking the root of the calendar lies in testing the qi.
translations.idiomatic: Heng held that the winter solstice is the foundation of any calendar, and that to find that foundation one must measure the seasonal qi.

sentences.zh: 今所用宋舊儀，自汴還至京師，已自乖舛，加之歲久，規環不葉。

translations.literal: The Song instruments now in use, moved from Bian to the capital, were already in error; added to this, years had passed and the rings and circles no longer matched.
translations.idiomatic: The Song instruments then in use had already been misaligned when moved from Kaifeng to the capital, and after years of wear their rings and circles no longer fit.

sentences.zh: 乃與太史令郭守敬等新制儀象圭表，自丙子之冬日測晷景，得丁丑、戊寅、己卯三年冬至加時，減《大明曆》十九刻二十分，又增損古歲餘歲差法，上考春秋以來冬至，無不盡合。

translations.literal: He thereupon together with Director of Astronomy Guo Shoujing and others newly made armillary spheres, celestial globes, and gnomon tables; from the winter of the bingzi year he measured shadow lengths, obtaining the winter solstice times for the three years dingchou, wuyin, and jimao—reducing the Great Enlightenment Calendar by nineteen quarters and twenty minutes—and also increased and decreased the ancient methods for annual remainder and precession; examining upward from the Spring and Autumn era, every winter solstice matched completely.
translations.idiomatic: With Director Guo Shoujing and others he built new armillary spheres, celestial globes, and gnomon tables. Beginning in the winter of the bingzi year he measured shadow lengths and fixed the winter solstice times for the three years dingchou, wuyin, and jimao—nineteen quarters and twenty minutes earlier than the Great Enlightenment Calendar predicted. He revised the ancient methods for annual remainder and precession, and checked every winter solstice back to the Spring and Autumn era; all matched.

sentences.zh: 以月食衝及金木二星距驗冬至日躔，校舊曆退七十六分。

translations.literal: Using lunar eclipses in opposition and the distances of the Metal and Wood planets to verify the winter solstice solar position, he corrected the old calendar by retreating seventy-six minutes.
translations.idiomatic: He verified the winter solstice solar position against lunar eclipses and the positions of Venus and Jupiter, correcting the old calendar by seventy-six minutes.

sentences.zh: 以日轉遲疾中平行度驗月離宿度，加舊曆三十刻。

translations.literal: Using the mean parallel degree at the midpoint of the sun's fast-slow motion to verify the moon's departure from lodge degrees, he added thirty quarters to the old calendar.
translations.idiomatic: He checked the moon's position against the sun's mean motion at the midpoint of its variable speed, adding thirty quarters to the old calendar.

sentences.zh: 以線代管窺測赤道宿度。

translations.literal: He used cords in place of tube-sights to measure equatorial lodge degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He measured equatorial lodge positions with cord sights in place of tube apertures.

sentences.zh: 以四正定氣立損益限，以定日之盈縮。

translations.literal: Using the four fixed seasonal qi he established limits of increase and decrease to fix the surplus and deficit of days.
translations.idiomatic: From the four fixed seasonal nodes he derived limits of increase and decrease to determine the varying length of days.

sentences.zh: 分二十八限為三百三十六，以定月之遲疾。

translations.literal: He divided twenty-eight limits into three hundred thirty-six to fix the moon's fast and slow motion.
translations.idiomatic: He subdivided the twenty-eight lunar stations into three hundred thirty-six intervals to fix the moon's variable speed.

sentences.zh: 以赤道變九道定月行。

translations.literal: Using the equator transformed into the nine paths, he fixed the moon's motion.
translations.idiomatic: He derived the moon's path from the equator through the nine celestial tracks.

sentences.zh: 以遲疾轉定度分定朔，而不用平行度。

translations.literal: Using fast-slow motion converted to fixed degrees and minutes he fixed the new moon, and did not use mean parallel degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed new moons from the moon's true rather than mean motion, converting variable speed into fixed degrees and minutes.

sentences.zh: 以日月實合時刻定晦，而不用虛進法。

translations.literal: Using the actual conjunction times of sun and moon he fixed the last day of the month, and did not use the fictitious advance method.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed month-end from the actual conjunction of sun and moon, abandoning the old fictitious advance method.

sentences.zh: 以躔離朓朒定交食。

translations.literal: Using solar and lunar positions together with the waning and waxing crescents, he fixed eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: From solar and lunar positions and the phases of the moon he calculated eclipses.

sentences.zh: 其法視古皆密，而又悉去諸歷積年月日法之傅會者，一本天道自然之數，可以施之永久而無弊。

translations.literal: Its methods, compared with antiquity, are all more precise; moreover it entirely removed the forced reconciliations of accumulated year-month-day methods in various calendars, taking as one root the natural numbers of the heavenly Way—able to be applied permanently without flaw.
translations.idiomatic: Its methods surpassed all earlier calendars in precision, and discarded the forced reconciliations that had accumulated in calendrical reckoning over the ages, resting instead on the natural numbers of heaven's way—a system that could endure forever without error.

sentences.zh: 自餘正訛完闕，蓋非一事。

translations.literal: Apart from this, corrections of errors and completion of gaps were not limited to one matter.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these reforms, errors were corrected and gaps filled in many other particulars.

sentences.zh: 十七年，歷成，奏上之，賜名曰《授時曆》，頒之天下。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the calendar was completed, submitted to the throne, granted the name Season-Granting Calendar, and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the calendar was finished and submitted. The Emperor named it the Season-Granting Calendar and promulgated it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 六月，以疾請還懷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, pleading illness, he requested to return to Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, citing illness, he asked to return to Huai.

sentences.zh: 皇太子為請於帝，以子師可為懷孟路總管以養之，且使東宮官來諭衡曰：「公毋以道不行為憂也，公安則道行有時矣，其善藥自愛。」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince pleaded with the Emperor on his behalf, appointing his son Shike Prefect of Huaimeng Circuit to support him, and also sent an Eastern Palace official to instruct Heng, saying, "Sir, do not grieve that the Way is not being put into practice; when you are secure, the Way will in time be put into practice—take good medicine and care for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince interceded with the Emperor, appointing Heng's son Shike prefect of Huaimeng Circuit to provide for him, and sent a palace officer with this message: "Do not grieve that the Way goes unheeded. When you are well, its hour will come. Take your medicine and tend to yourself.

sentences.zh: 十八年，衡病革，家人祠，衡曰：「吾一日未死，寧不有事於祖考。」

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Heng's illness became critical; the family performed sacrifice, and Heng said, "So long as I have not died for a single day, how could I fail to have affairs with my ancestors?
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, as Heng lay near death, his family began ancestral rites. Heng said, "While I still draw breath, how can I neglect my ancestors?

sentences.zh: 扶而起，奠獻如儀。

translations.literal: Supported, he rose and performed the offerings according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: They helped him rise, and he performed the offerings according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 既撤，家人餕，怡怡如也。

translations.literal: When the rites were withdrawn, the family partook of the sacrificial remains, and he was cheerful and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were done the family shared the sacrificial food, and he was serene and at peace.

sentences.zh: 已而卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 是日，大雷電，風拔木。

translations.literal: That day there was great thunder and lightning, and wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: That day thunder rolled across the sky and wind uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 懷人無貴賤少長，皆哭於門。

translations.literal: The people of Huai, without distinction of noble and base, young and old, all wept at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: People of Huai, high and low, young and old, wept at his gate.

sentences.zh: 四方學士聞訃，皆聚哭。

translations.literal: Scholars from the four quarters, hearing the obituary, all gathered to weep.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars from every quarter, hearing of his death, gathered to mourn.

sentences.zh: 有數千里來祭哭墓下者。

translations.literal: Some came several thousand li to offer sacrifice and weep at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Some traveled thousands of li to mourn and offer sacrifice at his grave.

sentences.zh: ○竇默李俊民附

translations.literal: Appendix: Dou Mo and Li Junmin
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Dou Mo and Li Junmin

sentences.zh: 竇默，字子聲，初名傑，字漢卿，廣平肥鄉人。

translations.literal: Dou Mo, courtesy name Zisheng, originally named Jie with courtesy name Hanqing, was a native of Feixiang in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Mo, whose courtesy name was Zisheng, was born Jie with the style Hanqing, a native of Feixiang in Guangping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼知讀書，毅然有立志。

translations.literal: From youth he knew how to read and was resolute in setting his will.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he took to books and set his heart on a purpose with quiet resolve.

sentences.zh: 族祖旺，為郡功曹，令習吏事，不肯就。

translations.literal: His clansman-ancestor Wang, who served as district merit officer, ordered him to study clerical affairs, but he refused to take it up.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Wang, a district merit officer, wanted him trained in official routine, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 會國兵伐金，默為所俘。

translations.literal: When the state's armies attacked Jin, Mo was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mongol armies invaded the Jin, Mo was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 同時被俘者三十人，皆見殺，惟默得脫，歸其鄉。

translations.literal: Thirty captives taken at the same time were all killed; only Mo escaped and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty captives taken with him were all killed; Mo alone escaped and made his way home.

sentences.zh: 家破，母獨存，驚怖之餘，母子俱得疾，母竟亡，扶病藁葬。

translations.literal: His household was ruined; only his mother survived. In the shock and terror, mother and son both fell ill; his mother finally died, and he, still sick, buried her in a straw coffin.
translations.idiomatic: His home lay in ruins; only his mother remained. Shaken by terror, they both fell ill. She died, and he buried her in a straw coffin while still sick himself.

sentences.zh: 而大兵復至，遂南走渡河，依母黨吳氏。

translations.literal: Then the great army came again; he fled south, crossed the river, and relied on the Wu clan, his mother's kin.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies returned he fled south across the river and took refuge with the Wu clan, his mother's kin.

sentences.zh: 醫者王翁妻以女，使業醫。

translations.literal: The physician Old Wang gave him his daughter in marriage and had him take up medicine as a profession.
translations.idiomatic: A physician named Wang gave him his daughter in marriage and set him to learn the medical arts.

sentences.zh: 轉客蔡州，遇名醫李浩，授以銅人針法。

translations.literal: Traveling as a guest to Cai Prefecture, he met the famed physician Li Hao, who taught him the bronze-figure needle method.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to Cai Prefecture, where the renowned physician Li Hao taught him acupuncture from the bronze figure.

sentences.zh: 金主遷蔡，默恐兵且至，又走​​德安。

translations.literal: When the Jin ruler moved to Cai, Mo feared the army would soon arrive and fled again to De'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin court moved to Cai, Mo feared the armies would follow and fled again to De'an.

sentences.zh: 孝感令謝憲子以伊洛性理之書授之，默自以為昔未嘗學，而學自此始。

translations.literal: Xie Xianzi, magistrate of Xiaogan, gave him books on the nature-and-principle learning of the Yi-Luo school; Mo considered that he had never studied before, and that study began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xianzi, magistrate of Xiaogan, introduced him to the Neo-Confucian texts of the Yi-Luo school. Mo felt he had never truly studied until then; his learning began at that moment.

sentences.zh: 適中書楊惟中奉旨招集儒、道、釋之士，默乃北歸，隱於大名，與姚樞、許衡朝暮講習，至忘寢食。

translations.literal: Just then Yang Weizhong of the Secretariat, by imperial order, gathered scholars of Confucianism, Daoism, and Buddhism; Mo thereupon returned north, concealed himself at Daming, and with Yao Shu and Xu Heng studied morning and evening until he forgot sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Weizhong of the Secretariat was ordered to gather scholars of Confucian, Daoist, and Buddhist learning, Mo returned north and settled quietly at Daming. There he studied day and night with Yao Shu and Xu Heng, forgetting sleep and meals.

sentences.zh: 繼還肥鄉，以經術教授，由是知名。

translations.literal: He afterward returned to Feixiang and taught the classics, and from this became known.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to Feixiang to teach the classics, and from that time his name spread.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛邸，遣召之，默變姓名以自晦。

translations.literal: When Shizu was in his princely residence, he sent to summon him; Mo changed his name to conceal himself.
translations.idiomatic: While Kublai was still heir apparent he sent for Mo, but Mo changed his name to keep out of sight.

sentences.zh: 使者俾其友人往見，而微服踵其後，默不得已，乃拜命。

translations.literal: The envoy had his friend go to see him, while he himself followed in plain dress; Mo had no choice and accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy sent a friend ahead while he himself followed in disguise. Mo could not evade him and accepted the summons.

sentences.zh: 既至，問以治道，默首以三綱五常為對。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was asked about the way of governance; Mo answered first with the Three Bonds and Five Constants.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was asked about governance. Mo answered first with the Three Bonds and Five Constants.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「人道之端，孰大於此。

translations.literal: Shizu said, "At the root of the human way, what is greater than this?
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "At the foundation of the human way, what could be greater than this?

sentences.zh: 失此，則無以立於世矣。」

translations.literal: Lose this, and there is no standing in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Without these, a man cannot stand in the world.

sentences.zh: 默又言：「帝王之道，在誠意正心，心既正，則朝廷遠近莫敢不一於正。」

translations.literal: Mo also said, "The way of emperors and kings lies in making the intent sincere and rectifying the heart; once the heart is rectified, then throughout the court, near and far, none dare fail to be of one rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Mo went on: "The way of kings lies in sincere intent and a rectified heart. Once the heart is right, court and realm alike will follow suit.

sentences.zh: 一日凡三召與語，奏對皆稱旨，自是敬待加禮，不令暫去左右。

translations.literal: In one day he was summoned three times to converse; his responses at audience all matched the imperial intent—from this he was treated with added respect and ceremony, and not allowed to leave the Prince's side even briefly.
translations.idiomatic: That day he was summoned three times; every answer pleased the Prince. From then on Kublai treated him with special honor and would not let him leave his side even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 世祖問今之明治道者，默薦姚樞，即召用之。

translations.literal: Shizu asked who today understood the way of good governance; Mo recommended Yao Shu, who was immediately summoned and employed.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai asked who best understood governance today, Mo recommended Yao Shu, who was summoned and appointed at once.

sentences.zh: 俄命皇子真金從默學，賜以玉帶鉤，諭之曰：「此金內府故物，汝老人，佩服為宜，且使我子見之如見我也。」

translations.literal: Soon he ordered Prince Zhenjin to study with Mo, and granted him a jade belt hook, instructing him, "This is an old treasure from Jin's inner palace. You are an elder—it is fitting that you wear it, and it will let my son see it as though seeing me."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kublai had Prince Zhenjin study under Mo and gave him a jade belt hook, saying, "This belonged to the Jin inner treasury. You are an elder—it suits you to wear it, and when my son sees it he will feel as though he sees me."

sentences.zh: 久之，請南還，命大名、順德各給田宅，有司歲具衣物以為常。

translations.literal: After a long time Mo requested to return south; he was ordered to be given fields and residences in Daming and Shunde respectively, and the officials were to prepare clothing yearly as a fixed provision.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Mo asked to return south. Kublai granted him fields and houses in Daming and Shunde and ordered officials to supply him with clothing every year as a permanent allowance.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，召至上都，問曰：「朕欲求如唐魏徵者，有其人乎？」

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, he summoned Mo to Shangdu and asked, "I wish to find someone like Tang's Wei Zheng—is there such a man?"
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai ascended the throne he summoned Mo to Shangdu and asked, "I want men like Wei Zheng of Tang. Are there any?"

sentences.zh: 默對曰：「犯顏諫諍，剛毅不屈，則許衡其人也。

translations.literal: Mo replied, "One who risks his countenance in frank remonstrance, upright and unyielding—that is Xu Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Mo answered, "For one who speaks bluntly to the ruler's face and will not bend—that is Xu Heng.

sentences.zh: 深識遠慮，有宰相才，則史天澤其人也。」

translations.literal: One of deep insight and far-reaching deliberation, with the talent of a chief minister—that is Shi Tianze."
translations.idiomatic: For deep insight, long planning, and ministerial talent—that is Shi Tianze."

sentences.zh: 天澤時宣撫河南，帝即召拜右丞相，以默為翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: Tianze was then pacification commissioner of Henan; the Emperor immediately summoned and appointed him Right Chancellor, and appointed Mo Hanlin Lecturing Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Tianze was serving as Henan pacification commissioner. The Emperor at once appointed him right chancellor and made Mo a Hanlin lecturing academician.

sentences.zh: 時初建中書省，平章政事王文統頗見委任，默上書曰：

translations.literal: At that time the Secretariat was newly established; Wang Wentshi, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, was greatly entrusted, and Mo submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat had just been established, and Wang Wentshi as grand councillor enjoyed broad trust. Mo submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣事陛下十有餘年，數承顧問，與聞聖訓，有以見陛下急於求治，未嘗不以利生民安社稷為心。

translations.literal: "Your subject has served Your Majesty more than ten years, repeatedly receiving your inquiries and hearing your sacred instructions, and thereby sees that Your Majesty is urgent in seeking good governance and never fails to take benefiting the people and securing the altars of soil and grain to heart.
translations.idiomatic: "I have served Your Majesty more than ten years, often consulted and hearing your instruction. I know how urgently you pursue good government—and I know your heart has never strayed from the welfare of the people and the security of the realm."

sentences.zh: 時先帝在上，奸臣擅權，總天下財賦，操執在手，貢進奇貨，炫耀紛華，以娛悅上心。

translations.literal: At that time the late emperor was still alive; wicked ministers monopolized power, gathered all the empire's wealth and taxes into their grip, presented strange goods as tribute, displayed glitter and splendor, and so pleased the sovereign's heart with entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: While the late emperor still reigned, corrupt ministers held power. They seized control of the empire's revenues, sent up exotic treasures, flaunted finery and display—and so won the sovereign's favor.

sentences.zh: 其扇結朋黨、離間骨肉者，皆此徒也。

translations.literal: Those who fanned factions, formed cliques, and estranged flesh and blood—all were this sort.
translations.idiomatic: The men who built factions and turned kin against kin were of that ilk.

sentences.zh: 此徒當路，陛下所以不能盡其初心。

translations.literal: While this sort held the road of office, Your Majesty could not fully carry out your original intent.
translations.idiomatic: As long as such men held sway, Your Majesty could not fully realize your original aims.

sentences.zh: 救世一念，涵養有年矣。

translations.literal: The single thought of saving the age has been nurtured for years.
translations.idiomatic: Your resolve to rescue the age has been gathering strength for years.

sentences.zh: 今天順人應，誕登大寶，天下生民，莫不歡忻踴躍，引領盛治。

translations.literal: Now Heaven accords and men respond; you have solemnly ascended the Great Treasure. All the living people under heaven none fail to rejoice and leap with joy, craning their necks toward magnificent governance.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven's mandate and the people's assent have brought you to the throne. Every subject under heaven rejoices and waits eagerly for an age of good rule.

sentences.zh: 然平治天下，必用正人端士，脣吻小人一時功利之說，必不能定立國家基本，為子孫久遠之計。

translations.literal: Yet to pacify and govern the realm, one must use upright men and principled scholars; the lip-serving petty men's talk of momentary profit and utility can by no means establish the foundations of the state or plan for the distant future of one's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to govern the realm well you must employ upright men of integrity. Smooth-talking schemers and their quick profits cannot lay the foundations of state or secure your descendants' future.

sentences.zh: 其賣利獻勤、乞憐取寵者，使不得行其志，斯可矣。

translations.literal: As for those who sell profit and offer diligence, beg pity and seek favor—simply let them not carry out their designs, and that will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Keep those who trade favor for profit and fawn for preferment from having their way—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 若夫鉤距揣摩，以利害驚動人主之意者，無他，意在擯斥諸賢，獨執政柄耳，此蘇、張之流也，惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: As for those who probe and conjecture, startling the ruler's mind with benefit and harm—there is nothing else to it: their intent is to drive out worthy men and hold the governing handle alone. These are men in the mold of Su Qin and Zhang Yi. I pray Your Majesty discern them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who probe motives and alarm the throne with threats and promises seek one thing only: to drive out the worthy and keep power to themselves. They are Su Qin and Zhang Yi reborn. I beg Your Majesty to see through them.

sentences.zh: 伏望別選公明有道之士，授以重任，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself in hope that Your Majesty will separately select fair-minded men possessed of the Way and entrust them with heavy responsibilities—then all under heaven will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly ask that you choose clear-sighted men of the Way and give them real authority. The realm would be the better for it.

sentences.zh: 他日，默與王鶚、姚樞俱在帝前，复面斥文統曰：「此人學術不正，久居相位，必禍天下。」

translations.literal: Another day, Mo together with Wang E and Yao Shu were all before the Emperor; Mo again openly denounced Wentshi, saying, "This man's learning is not upright; long occupying the post of chief minister, he will surely bring calamity on the realm."
translations.idiomatic: On another day Mo stood before the Emperor with Wang E and Yao Shu and again openly denounced Wentshi: "His scholarship is unsound. Leave him long as chief minister and he will ruin the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然則誰可相者？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Then who could serve as chief minister?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "Then who is fit to be chief minister?"

sentences.zh: 默曰： 「以臣觀之，無如許衡。」

translations.literal: Mo said, "In your subject's view, none compares to Xu Heng."
translations.idiomatic: Mo said, "In my view, no one compares to Xu Heng."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅而罷。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased and dismissed the audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased and cut the conversation short.

sentences.zh: 文統深忌之，乃請以默為太子太傅，默辭曰：「太子位號未正，臣不敢先受太傅之名。」

translations.literal: Wentshi deeply resented him and therefore requested that Mo be made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent. Mo declined, saying, "The Heir Apparent's title and rank are not yet fixed; your subject dare not first accept the name of Grand Tutor."
