translations.idiomatic: Wentshi hated him bitterly and proposed making Mo grand tutor of the heir apparent. Mo refused: "The heir's rank is not yet formally established—I dare not take the title of grand tutor first."

sentences.zh: 乃復以為翰林侍講學士，詳見《許衡傳》 。

translations.literal: He was then again appointed Hanlin Lecturing Academician—see the "Biography of Xu Heng" in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was reappointed Hanlin lecturing academician instead. See the Biography of Xu Heng for particulars.

sentences.zh: 默俄謝病歸，未幾，文統伏誅，帝追憶其言，謂近臣曰：「曩言王文統不可用者，惟竇漢卿一人。

translations.literal: Mo soon took leave on grounds of illness and returned home. Before long Wentshi suffered execution. The Emperor recalled his words and said to close ministers, "Of those who earlier said Wang Wentshi could not be used, only Dou Hanqing was one.
translations.idiomatic: Mo soon retired on grounds of illness. Before long Wentshi was executed. Remembering Mo's warnings, the Emperor told his close advisers, "Of those who warned me against Wang Wentshi, only Dou Hanqing spoke out.

sentences.zh: 向使更有一二人言之，朕寧不之思耶？」

translations.literal: If one or two more had spoken thus, would I not have reflected on it?"
translations.idiomatic: Had one or two others spoken as he did, would I not have taken heed?

sentences.zh: 召還，賜第京師，命有司月給廩祿，國有大政，輒以訪之。

translations.literal: He was recalled, granted a residence in the capital, ordered that officials monthly supply official salary, and whenever the state had great affairs of government, Mo was consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was recalled, given a house in the capital, and granted a monthly stipend. On major state matters the Emperor sought his counsel.

sentences.zh: 默與王磐等請分置翰林院，專掌蒙古文字，以翰林學士承旨撒的迷底里主之；

translations.literal: Mo together with Wang Pan and others requested that the Hanlin Academy be separately established to manage exclusively Mongol script, with Hanlin Academician Chancellor Sadmiji as its head;
translations.idiomatic: Mo and Wang Pan petitioned to split off a Hanlin academy devoted solely to the Mongol script, under Chancellor Sadmiji;

sentences.zh: 其翰林兼國史院，仍舊纂修國史，典制誥，備顧問，以翰林學士承旨兼修起居注和禮霍孫主之。

translations.literal: the Hanlin Academy combined with the National History Academy would as before compile the national history, manage edicts and decrees, and serve for consultation, with Hanlin Academician Chancellor Hezhesun, who also kept the diurnal records, as its head.
translations.idiomatic: while the existing Hanlin-and-national-history office would continue compiling the dynastic history, drafting edicts, and serving as advisers—under Chancellor Hezhesun, who also kept the court diary.

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 默又言：「三代所以風俗淳厚、歷數長久者，皆設學養士所致。

translations.literal: Mo also said, "The reason the Three Dynasties had pure and generous customs and long-enduring reigns was entirely because they established schools and nurtured scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Mo added, "The Three Dynasties endured because their customs were strong—and that came of founding schools and nurturing scholars.

sentences.zh: 今宜建學立師，博選貴族子弟教之，以示風化之本。」

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to establish schools and appoint teachers, broadly select nobles' sons to teach them, thereby showing the root of transformation by instruction."
translations.idiomatic: You should establish schools and teachers now, choose widely among the sons of the nobility, and show where cultural renewal begins.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor warmly accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 默嘗與劉秉忠、姚樞、劉肅、商挺侍上前，默言：「君有過舉，臣當直言，都俞籲咈，古之所尚。

translations.literal: Mo once with Liu Bingzhong, Yao Shu, Liu Su, and Shang Ting attended before the Emperor; Mo said, "When the ruler has a faulty act, ministers should speak directly—'Yes, yes,' 'Ah, no!'—such was what antiquity honored.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending the Emperor with Liu Bingzhong, Yao Shu, Liu Su, and Shang Ting, Mo said, "When a ruler errs, his ministers must speak plainly. Open debate between ruler and minister is the ancient ideal.

sentences.zh: 今則不然，君曰可，臣亦以為可，君曰否，臣亦以為否，非善政也。」

translations.literal: Today it is not so: the ruler says yes and ministers also say yes; the ruler says no and ministers also say no—it is not good government."
translations.idiomatic: Today it is otherwise: the ruler says yes and every minister says yes; the ruler says no and every minister says no. That is not good government.

sentences.zh: 明日，復侍帝於幄殿。

translations.literal: The next day he again attended the Emperor in the curtain hall.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he attended the Emperor again in the tent palace.

sentences.zh: 獵者失一鶻，帝怒，侍臣或從旁大聲謂宜加罪。

translations.literal: A huntsman lost a hawk; the Emperor was angry, and attending ministers some from the side loudly said punishment should be imposed.
translations.idiomatic: A falconer lost a hawk. The Emperor was furious, and some courtiers loudly urged that the man be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其迎合，命杖之，釋獵者不問。

translations.literal: The Emperor disliked their pandering, ordered them beaten with rods, and released the huntsman without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Disgusted by their sycophancy, the Emperor had those courtiers beaten and let the falconer go.

sentences.zh: 既退，秉忠等賀默曰：「非公誠結主知，安得感悟至此。」

translations.literal: After withdrawing, Bingzhong and others congratulated Mo, saying, "Had it not been for your sincerity winning the sovereign's understanding, how could enlightenment have reached this point?"
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Liu Bingzhong and the others congratulated Mo: "But for your sincerity and the trust you win from the sovereign, he would never have been moved this far."

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，默年八十，公卿皆往賀，帝聞之，拱手曰：「此輩賢者，安得請於上帝，減去數年，留朕左右，共治天下，惜今老矣！」

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, Mo was eighty; the dukes and ministers all went to congratulate him. When the Emperor heard, he clasped his hands and said, "These worthy men—how could one beg Heaven to subtract a few years and keep them at my side to govern the realm together? Alas, they are old now!"
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 12, when Mo turned eighty, the high ministers all came to congratulate him. Hearing of it, the Emperor said with folded hands, "Men such as these—if only one could ask Heaven to grant a few more years and keep them at my side to help rule the realm! But they are old now.

sentences.zh: 悵然者久之。

translations.literal: He was wistful a long while.
translations.idiomatic: He lingered in regret a long while.

sentences.zh: 默既老，不視事，帝數遣中使以珍玩及諸器物往存問焉。

translations.literal: Once Mo was old he no longer handled affairs; the Emperor repeatedly sent palace envoys with precious curios and various objects to visit and inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: In his old age Mo no longer took office, but the Emperor often sent palace eunuchs with rare gifts and furnishings to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 十七年，加昭文館大學士，卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall; he died at age eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall. He died at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，帝深為嗟悼，厚加賵賜，皇太子亦賻以鈔二千貫，命有司護送歸葬肥鄉。

translations.literal: When the death report arrived, the Emperor deeply sighed in grief, generously added funeral gifts, the Crown Prince also contributed two thousand strings of paper money, and officials were ordered to escort the body home for burial at Feixiang.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death arrived, the Emperor mourned deeply and gave lavish funeral gifts. The crown prince sent two thousand strings of paper cash, and officials were ordered to escort the body home to Feixiang for burial.

sentences.zh: 默為人樂易，平居未嘗評品人物，與人居，溫然儒者也。

translations.literal: Mo as a man was easy-going; in ordinary life he never ranked and appraised people; with others he was always gently the scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was easy in temperament. In daily life he never ranked people; in company he was always the gentle scholar.

sentences.zh: 至論國家大計，面折廷諍，人謂汲黯無以過之。

translations.literal: When it came to discussing great plans of state, he would openly oppose and remonstrate at court—people said even Ji An could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet on matters of state he would debate openly at court, and many said Ji An himself could not have outdone him.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂侍臣曰：「朕求賢三十年，惟得竇漢卿及李​​俊民二人。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once said to attending ministers, "I have sought worthies thirty years and obtained only Dou Hanqing and Li Junmin—two men."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once told his ministers, "In thirty years of seeking talent I have found only two men—Dou Hanqing and Li Junmin.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「如竇漢卿之心，姚公茂之才，合而為一，斯可謂全人矣。」

translations.literal: He also said, "If one had Dou Hanqing's heart and Yao Gongmao's talent combined in one person, that could be called a complete man."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Combine Dou Hanqing's character with Yao Shu's talent, and you would have a whole man."

sentences.zh: 後累贈太師，封魏國公，諡文正。

translations.literal: Later, through successive posthumous promotions he was given Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously promoted to grand preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, and given the posthumous name Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 子履，集賢大學士。

translations.literal: His son Lü served as Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lü became grand academician of the Jixian Hall.

sentences.zh: 李俊民，字用章，澤州人。

translations.literal: Li Junmin, courtesy name Yongzhang, was a native of Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Junmin, style Yongzhang, was from Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 得河南程氏傳受之學。

translations.literal: He obtained the transmitted learning of the Cheng school of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He received the Cheng school Neo-Confucian teaching from Henan.

sentences.zh: 金承安中，舉進士第一，應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: In the Cheng'an era of Jin, he placed first in the jinshi examination and served as Hanlin Composition Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin Cheng'an era he placed first on the jinshi examination and served as Hanlin composition attendant.

sentences.zh: 未幾，棄官不仕，以所學教授鄉里，從之者甚盛，至有不遠千里而來者。

translations.literal: Before long he abandoned office and would not serve, using what he had learned to teach in his home district; followers were very numerous, even to the point of some coming from a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he quit office and taught in his home district. His following grew large—some came from a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 金源南遷，隱於嵩山，後徙懷州，俄复隱於西山。

translations.literal: When the Jin court moved south, he concealed himself on Mount Song; afterward he moved to Huai Prefecture, and soon again concealed himself on the Western Hills.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin moved south he withdrew to Mount Song, later moved to Huai Prefecture, and soon retreated again to the Western Hills.

sentences.zh: 既而變起倉猝，人服其先知。

translations.literal: Before long upheaval arose in sudden haste, and people admired his prior knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: When turmoil broke out suddenly, people marveled at his foresight.

sentences.zh: 俊民在河南時，隱士荊先生者，授以邵雍《皇極》數。

translations.literal: When Junmin was in Henan, a recluse Master Jing taught him Shao Yong's numerology of the Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: While in Henan, a recluse known as Master Jing taught him Shao Yong's numerology of the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 時之知數者，無出劉秉忠之右，亦自以為弗及也。

translations.literal: Of those who understood numerology at the time, none surpassed Liu Bingzhong; Junmin himself also considered he did not reach that level.
translations.idiomatic: Among numerologists of the day none surpassed Liu Bingzhong—and Junmin thought himself no equal to Liu either.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛籓，以安車召之，延訪無虛日。

translations.literal: When Shizu was in his latent fief, he summoned him with the comfort carriage; consultations extended with no idle day.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, Kublai summoned him with a carriage of honor and consulted him nearly every day.

sentences.zh: 遽乞還山，世祖重違其意，遣中貴人護送之。

translations.literal: He suddenly begged to return to the mountains; Shizu greatly loathed to go against his wish and sent a palace favorite to escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to return to his mountain retreat. Reluctant to refuse, Kublai sent a eunuch to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 又嘗令張仲一問以禎祥，及即位，其言皆驗。

translations.literal: He also once had Zhang Zhongyi question him on auspicious and ominous signs; when the Emperor took the throne, his words all proved true.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Zhang Zhongyi consult Li on omens and portents—and when Kublai took the throne, every prediction proved true.

sentences.zh: 而俊民已死，賜諡莊靜先生。

translations.literal: But Junmin had already died; he was granted the posthumous honorific Master Zhuangjing.
translations.idiomatic: By then Li Junmin was already dead. He was posthumously honored as Master Zhuangjing.
